The first session focused on physical assessment and individual drills. Speed. Footwork. Shooting accuracy. Defensive positioning.

Yichen moved with a level of intensity Xiaoran rarely saw outside important games. He didn’t waste movement. He didn’t complain.

When he missed a shot, he retrieved the ball and repeated the attempt.

When the coach corrected his footwork, he listened and adjusted.

When another player challenged him during a defensive drill, he responded immediately. He was competitive. Quietly, relentlessly competitive.

Xiaoran watched him and felt her chest swell with pride, then came the scrimmage. The players were divided into teams.

Yichen was assigned to a group with several athletes who had already played at a higher level. At first, he seemed to be observing. Learning their rhythm. Understanding how they moved. Then he began to adapt. He found passing lanes. Anticipated defensive movements. Created space.

And when the opportunity came, he drove towards the basket and scored. The coach called out something. Yichen nodded. He was sweating heavily now.

His breathing had become more pronounced, but his focus never wavered.

Xiaoran found herself gripping the edge of her seat.

A player from the opposing team made a sharp move, trying to get past him. Yichen intercepted. The ball changed possession. He passed it forward. His teammate scored. Xiaoran almost stood up. She caught herself at the last second.

Then she whispered, “That’s my boyfriend.”

A woman sitting two seats away glanced at her and smiled. Xiaoran immediately looked down. The trial ended late in the afternoon.

Yichen walked towards the changing rooms with the other players. Xiaoran waited.

She had sent him a message earlier, but he hadn’t checked his phone.

When he finally came out, his hair was damp, his shoulders slightly slumped from exhaustion, and his expression unreadable. She stood immediately.

“How was it?”

He took the bag she was holding.

“Long.”

“That’s all?”

“Very long.”

She looked at his face.

“Are you okay?”

“I’m fine.”

“Did you enjoy it?”

He considered the question.

“Yes.”

Her smile returned.

“Really?”

“It’s different.”

“Different good or different bad?”

“Different challenging.”

She nodded. He took her hand.

“Let’s get something to eat.”

She walked beside him, but she couldn’t help looking at him. He seemed quieter than usual. Not upset. Just thoughtful.

After a few minutes, she asked, “Do you think you did well?”

He glanced at her.

“I think I did what I could.”

“That’s not what I asked.”

He smiled faintly.

“Then yes. I think I did well.”

She squeezed his hand.

“Good.”

He looked at her.

“You’re very quiet.”

“I’m trying not to ask a hundred questions.”

“That’s considerate.”

“I have at least two hundred.”

He laughed.

“Save them for dinner.”

✦ ✦ ✦

The call came three days later. Yichen was at home when his phone rang. He listened carefully.

Xiaoran was sitting on the sofa, pretending to read.

She had been pretending for the past fifteen minutes.

When he ended the call, she immediately looked up.

“What happened?”

He sat down beside her.

“The club wants me to come back for another evaluation.”

Her face lit up.

“Really?”

“There’s a second stage. They’ll assess how I perform with the main training group.”

She put her book down.

“Yichen!”

He smiled. She grabbed his arm.

“That’s good, isn’t it?”

“It is.”

“That’s really good!”

He laughed as she threw her arms around him.

She hugged him so tightly that he had to lean back against the sofa.

“Congratulations!”

“Thank you.”

“I knew you’d get it.”

He rested his chin against her head.

“Thank you.”

She pulled away.

“Are you happy?”

“Yes. A little nervous about the next stage.”

She nodded.

“That’s normal.”

“Mm.”

She studied his face.

“You’ll do well.”

“You’re very confident.”

“Of course. I’ve seen you play.”

He reached up and tucked a strand of hair behind her ear.

“And if I don’t?”

She frowned.

“Then you’ll still be Zhou Yichen.”

He looked at her. She continued, as if explaining something obvious.

“You’ll still be the person who studies business, makes fun of my cooking, steals my drinks, and pretends he doesn’t like being hugged.”

“I don’t pretend.”

“You do.”

“Never.”

She smiled.

“And you’ll still be my boyfriend.”

His expression softened. She touched his cheek.

“Getting selected would be wonderful. But it doesn’t change what I think of you.”

He said nothing. Then he leaned forward and kissed her cheek. He crooked a finger at her. She went willingly.

He held her against him, one hand resting at the back of her head.

“Do you know something?” he murmured.

“What?”

“When I first started playing basketball seriously, I thought the best part would be getting better.”

She looked up.

“And now?”

“Now I think the best part is having someone to tell when something good happens.”

Her expression softened.

“Then tell me everything.”

“I will.”

“Even the boring parts.”

“Especially the boring parts.”

She nodded, satisfied. Then she remembered something.

“Wait.”

He looked down.

“What?”

“Does this mean I have to learn how professional basketball works?”

He laughed.

“You don’t have to.”

“But I want to understand.”

“You already understand more than you think.”

“Really?”

“Mm.”

She looked pleased.

“Then next time, I’ll sit with the serious expression.”

He raised an eyebrow.

“You already do that.”

“Because I’m naturally intelligent.”

“Of course.”

“And the girlfriend of a very handsome boyfriend.”

He laughed, pulling her closer.

“That’s a very important qualification.”

She grinned. Then she kissed his cheek. He turned his head slightly and caught her lips instead. When he pulled away, she blinked.

“That’s cheating.”

He smiled, looking entirely unrepentant.

“Then I suppose I’ll do it again.”

And he kissed her once more. Outside, the evening settled over the campus.

Somewhere across the city, a professional club was reviewing footage of a university player they had noticed at the back of a gym.

They had seen his speed, his discipline, his court awareness, and his competitive instincts. They had seen a young athlete with potential.

But they hadn’t seen the boy who carefully saved a miniature basketball keychain because his girlfriend had given it to him.

They hadn’t seen the way he checked his phone after every session, hoping to find a message from her.

They hadn’t seen how, after years of working towards something, he had finally begun to imagine what his future might look like.

And, for the first time, that future was beginning to look a little bigger than the university gym. Yichen didn’t know yet where it would lead.

But when Xiaoran tucked herself against his shoulder and asked whether he wanted her to come to the next evaluation, he answered without hesitation.

“Of course.”

She smiled.

“Then I’ll be there.”

He kissed her hair.

“I know.”

chapters.desc: While he talks to his coach, a recruiter sits down beside Lin Xiaoran and asks a few questions. She answers every single one.
chapters.title: The Girlfriend Who Didn’t Know She Was Being Interviewed
chapters.epigraph: “That’s why they should ask me.”
chapters.content:
By the time the second evaluation ended, Xiaoran had developed a specific understanding of professional basketball.

It involved a lot of running, a lot of shouting, an unreasonable number of whistles, and Zhou Yichen looking so handsome that she sometimes forgot what she was supposed to be watching.

She was beginning to suspect that the last part was a personal problem.

The evaluation had lasted nearly three hours. Unlike the first session, this one had included practice with the club’s main training group. The pace was faster, the players were stronger, and the coaches seemed considerably less interested in offering encouragement. Yichen had been focused from beginning to end.

He wasn’t the loudest player on the court. He didn’t celebrate every successful play or complain when a teammate made a mistake. He simply adjusted, observed, and played. And Xiaoran had noticed something else.

When he was challenged, he became even more composed. It was almost annoying.

She had watched him lose possession once, recover immediately, and make a defensive play that earned an approving nod from one of the coaches. Later, when he missed a difficult shot, he didn’t look frustrated. He simply retrieved the ball and tried again.

By the time the session ended, Xiaoran was practically glowing with pride.

She waited near the entrance with his water bottle and a small towel.

When Yichen finally walked over, she handed them to him.

“Here.”

“Thank you.”

“You were good.”

He wiped his face. “Just good?”

She tilted her head.

“Very good.”

“Better.”

He took the water bottle from her and drank half of it before asking, “How long have you been waiting?”

“Not long.”

“Xiaoran.”

“Twenty minutes.”

He glanced at the clock.

“Practice ended ten minutes ago.”

“I know.”

“So?”

She smiled innocently.

“I was enjoying the atmosphere.”

He looked at the empty corridor, then back at her.

“Of course.”

She took the towel from his hand and folded it over her arm.

“Are you tired?”

“A little.”

“Hungry?”

“Very.”

“Good. I found a restaurant nearby.”

He raised an eyebrow.

“You found it?”

“I researched.”

“Should I be concerned?”

“Why?”

“Your research sometimes involves choosing restaurants based on how pretty the desserts look.”

“That’s a perfectly valid research method.”

He laughed and gently touched her hair.

“Give me ten minutes. I need to speak with Coach.”

“Okay.”

“Stay here.”

She nodded. He walked back towards the training area.

Xiaoran found a seat near the hallway and began looking through her phone, completely unaware that someone had been observing her for the past few minutes.

“Excuse me.”

She looked up. A man in his late thirties stood a short distance away. He wore a dark polo shirt with the club’s logo embroidered on the chest and held a tablet.

“Are you waiting for Zhou Yichen?”

“Yes.”

“I’m with the club’s recruitment department. My name is Jiao Rui.”

Xiaoran immediately stood.

“Oh, hello.”

He smiled politely.

“You’re his girlfriend, right?”

She blinked, then nodded.

“Yes.”

“I’m sorry to interrupt. I wanted to ask you something, if you don’t mind.”

“Of course.”

He gestured towards the empty seat beside her.

“May I?”

She nodded again. Jiao Rui sat down.

“I’ve seen you at both evaluation sessions.”

Xiaoran looked slightly surprised.

“Really?”

“You’re quite attentive.”

She laughed awkwardly.

“I’m just watching my boyfriend.”

“That’s precisely why I’d like to ask you a few questions.”

She didn’t think much of it. After all, he worked for the club. Perhaps he wanted to know more about Yichen’s university background, or whether Yichen had any particular preferences regarding training schedules. She straightened a little.

“Sure.”

Jiao Rui glanced at his tablet.

“What do you think of Zhou Yichen as a player?”

Xiaoran paused. Then she smiled.

“Oh.”

She seemed relieved.

“That’s easy.”

Jiao Rui smiled back. She thought for a moment.

“Very good.”

He waited. She looked at him.

“What?”

“Could you tell me a little more?”

Xiaoran nodded seriously.

“Of course.”

She turned slightly towards the court, where a few players were still practising.

“First, I think he’s very observant. He doesn’t always immediately react to what’s happening. Sometimes he watches for a moment before deciding what to do. I think that’s one of his strengths.”

Jiao Rui began typing.

“And?”

“He adapts quickly. I noticed it today. The first time he played with the group, he was still figuring out everyone’s rhythm. But today, he seemed much more comfortable.”

“Interesting.”

“And he’s very disciplined.”

“How so?”

“He doesn’t like wasting time.”

She smiled.

“Actually, sometimes I think he’s a little too disciplined.”

Jiao Rui looked up.

“Too disciplined?”

“Mm. If he has something he wants to improve, he’ll keep doing it until he’s satisfied. Even when he’s already tired.”

She hesitated.

“Although I’m not sure whether that’s a bad thing for a player.”

Jiao Rui shook his head.

“Not necessarily.”

Xiaoran nodded.

“I think it’s good. But he also needs to know when to rest.”

Jiao Rui typed something else.

“Do you think he’s competitive?”

She almost laughed.

“Very.”

“Can you elaborate?”

Xiaoran looked at him with an expression of absolute sincerity.

“Have you seen him play?”

Jiao Rui laughed.

“I have.”

“Then you probably already know.”

He smiled.

“Still, I’d like to hear your perspective.”

She considered it.

“He doesn’t necessarily show it in the way people expect. He doesn’t need to talk about winning all the time. But once he’s playing, he really wants to win.”

She paused.

“Sometimes he gets this expression…”

“What expression?”

She tried to imitate Yichen’s focused face, narrowing her eyes and pressing her lips together. Jiao Rui laughed.

“Like that?”

“Yes!”

She nodded enthusiastically.

“That’s the expression. When he looks like that, I usually know I shouldn’t disturb him.”

“Does he get frustrated when things don’t go his way?”

“He does, but he doesn’t take it out on other people.”

Her answer came quickly.

“He might be unhappy with himself, but he doesn’t blame his teammates. At least, I’ve never seen him do that.”

Jiao Rui looked at her.

“And what would you say is his biggest weakness?”

Xiaoran fell silent. This question required more thought. She looked down at her hands.

“Maybe…”

She frowned.

“He can be a little too hard on himself.”

Jiao Rui waited.

“Sometimes, when he makes a mistake, he doesn’t seem satisfied even after correcting it. He’ll keep thinking about it.”

She looked up.

“I don’t think he’s afraid of failing. I think he just has very high expectations of himself.”

Jiao Rui nodded slowly.

“And outside the court?”

Xiaoran blinked.

“Outside?”

“Yes. What is he like?”

She smiled almost immediately.

“Very different.”

“How so?”

“He’s quiet. He’s actually quite patient, although he pretends he’s not.”

Jiao Rui looked amused.

“Pretends?”

“Yes.”

She seemed increasingly comfortable now.

“He’s also very attentive. He remembers things people tell him, even when they don’t think he’s listening. He’s good at noticing small changes.”

“Does that translate into his relationships with teammates?”

“I think so.”

She nodded.

“He doesn’t always say much, but he pays attention. I think he’s the kind of person who notices when someone isn’t doing well.”

Jiao Rui made another note.

“Would you say he’s a leader?”

Xiaoran thought carefully.

“Not because he wants everyone to listen to him.”

She smiled.

“I think he leads more through what he does. He takes responsibility. He doesn’t expect other people to work harder than he does.”

Jiao Rui looked up.

“That’s a strong endorsement.”

Xiaoran laughed.

“I’m his girlfriend. I’m supposed to say nice things.”

“Would you say these things if you weren’t?”

She paused. Then her expression became a little more serious.

“Yes.”

“Why?”

“Because they’re true.”

There was no hesitation.

She said, “I don’t think you should select him just because I’m saying he’s wonderful. You should watch him play. Watch how he responds when he’s tired, when he’s behind, when someone makes a mistake, or when he doesn’t get the ball.” She glanced towards the court.

“Those things tell you more about a person.”

Jiao Rui stopped typing. For the first time, he looked at her with something more than polite interest.

“That’s a good point.”

Xiaoran smiled.

“Thank you.”

He studied her for another moment.

“Do you think he wants to become a professional player?”

Her smile softened.

“Yes.”

“Are you certain?”

“Very.”

“How do you know?”

She looked down briefly.

“Because I’ve seen how he works for it.”

Then she looked back at Jiao Rui.

“He doesn’t talk about it all the time. But I know it’s important to him.”

She paused.

“And I think he’d regret not trying.”

Jiao Rui nodded.

“Would you support him if it meant a significant change in his life?”

“Of course.”

“Even if it meant moving to another city one day?”

“Yes.”

“Even if his schedule became more demanding?”

She smiled.

“I’d probably complain about how little time I get with him.”

Jiao Rui laughed.

“But you’d support him?”

“Absolutely.”

She said it so naturally that Jiao Rui didn’t need to ask again.

“His career belongs to him. I want him to have the chance to find out how far he can go,” she said. She looked at the man.

“I don’t want him to look back one day and wonder what would have happened if he’d tried.”

Jiao Rui’s expression became thoughtful. Then he closed his tablet.

“Thank you, Miss Lin.”

She nodded.

“Of course.”

He stood.

“And I hope you continue supporting him.”

Xiaoran smiled.

“I will.”

He took a few steps away before turning back.

“One more thing.”

“Yes?”

“Has Zhou Yichen ever told you about his expectations for this opportunity?”

She considered it.

“He wants to do well. But I don’t think he’s assuming anything will happen.”

Jiao Rui smiled.

“That’s good.”

Then he walked away. Xiaoran watched him disappear down the corridor. She sat back down. Then she opened her phone.

Xiaoran: Yichen.

Xiaoran: I just spoke to someone from your club.

Xiaoran: I think he was asking about you.

Xiaoran: I said you’re very good.

She considered that, then sent another message.

Xiaoran: And handsome.

Yichen returned about five minutes later. He found her sitting in the same place, looking rather pleased with herself.

“Who were you talking to?”

She looked up.

“Someone from the recruitment department.”

He stopped.

“Jiao Rui?”

“Yes! You know him?”

Yichen placed his sports bag beside the seat.

“He’s one of the people overseeing the evaluation.”

“Oh.”

He looked at her.

“What did he want?”

“To ask me some questions.”

Yichen’s expression remained neutral.

“What questions?”

She began counting on her fingers.

“What I think of you as a player. Your strengths. Your weaknesses. Whether you’re competitive. What you’re like outside the court. Whether you want to become a professional player.”

Yichen stared at her. She smiled.

“He asked quite a lot.”

A pause.

Then Yichen asked, “And what did you say?”

She looked offended.

“Obviously, I said good things.”

“Obviously?”

“Do you think I’d tell him you’re annoying?”

He tilted his head. He laughed. She reached for her bag.

“Come on. I’m hungry.”

But Yichen hadn’t moved. He was looking at her with a slightly different expression now.

“Xiaoran.”

“What?”

“Did you know he was evaluating you?”

She stopped. Her brows drew together.

“What?”

“He was interviewing you.”

She blinked, then blinked again.

“Interviewing me?”

“Mm.”

“For what?”

“To see what kind of person you are.”

She stared at him. Then slowly looked in the direction Jiao Rui had disappeared.

“Wait.”

Yichen watched her.

“Wait, wait, wait.”

She turned back.

“He was interviewing me?”

“That’s what it sounds like.”

“About you?”

“Yes.”

She opened her mouth. Closed it, then opened it again.

“Why didn’t you tell me?”

Yichen smiled.

“You didn’t ask.”

“Yichen!”

He laughed. She covered her face with both hands.

“Oh my god.”

He reached over and gently pulled one hand away.

“What?”

“I was talking so much.”

“I noticed.”

“I told him you were too disciplined.”

“You weren’t wrong.”

“I said you had a scary face when you’re competitive.”

“Also not wrong.”

“I told him you were patient.”

He raised an eyebrow.

“Were you lying?”

“Don’t make this worse.”

He laughed again. She remembered something.

“And I told him you’re handsome.”

His smile became more pronounced.

“Did you?”

“Yes.”

“Good.”

She looked at him in disbelief.

“That’s all you have to say?”

“What else should I say?”

“You should be embarrassed!”

“Why?”

“Because I said it to someone from your workplace!”

He leaned closer.

“Would you prefer I tell him you’re beautiful?”

She froze. He smiled.

“Would that be embarrassing?”

Her cheeks warmed.

“That’s different.”

“How?”

“Because…”

She struggled to find an answer. Yichen watched her with quiet amusement.

Then he reached over, gently brushed a loose strand of hair away from her face, and pressed a kiss into her hair.

“Thank you.”

She looked up.

“For what?”

“For saying those things.”

Her expression softened.

“I meant them.”

“I know.”

He took her hand.

“And for what it’s worth, I think you gave him a better answer than I would have.”

She looked surprised.

“Really?”

“Mm.”

“What would you have said?”

He considered it.

“I’m hardworking. I want to improve. I’m competitive. I can adapt.”

“That’s very you.”

“And I would have probably forgotten to mention that I don’t blame my teammates.”

She smiled.

“See? That’s why they should ask me.”

He laughed.

“Apparently.”

✦ ✦ ✦

They were halfway to the restaurant when Yichen’s phone rang. It was Jiao Rui. Yichen answered.

“Hello.”

“Zhou Yichen. Sorry to call you after the session.”

“It’s fine.”

“I wanted to let you know that the recruitment team has completed its initial discussion.”

Yichen slowed his pace. Xiaoran glanced at him.

“We’d like to invite you to the next stage of the process. There are still several assessments ahead, but your performance today was encouraging,” Jiao Rui said.

Yichen listened carefully.

“Thank you. I appreciate the opportunity.”

“We’ll send the schedule and details tomorrow.”

“Understood.”

The call ended. Xiaoran immediately looked at him.

“Well?”

He turned towards her.

“They want me to proceed to the next stage.”

Her face lit up.

“Yichen!”

He smiled. She grabbed his arm.

“That’s amazing!”

“It’s good news.”

“It’s very good news!”

He laughed as she bounced slightly on her heels. Then she stopped.

“Wait.”

“What?”

“Does that mean my interview helped?”

He looked at her.

“Maybe.”

Her eyes widened.

“Really?”

“Perhaps they liked your answers.”

She looked extremely pleased with herself.

“I knew it.”

He raised an eyebrow.

“You knew what?”

“That I was a good candidate.”

He laughed.

“You weren’t the one being evaluated.”

“Apparently, I was.”

He took her hand and started walking again.

“Then congratulations.”

“Thank you.”

“Should I buy you dinner to celebrate?”

She looked at him.

“Obviously.”

“Anything you want.”

She thought for a moment.

“Crayfish. The spicy kind.”

“Fine.”

“And dessert.”

“Fine.”

“And you have to tell me what the next stage involves.”

“I’ll tell you when I know.”

“And I want to know what they thought of my answers.”

He smiled.

“Very curious.”

“Of course. I’ve invested in this recruitment process.”

“Have you?”

“Emotionally.”

He laughed.

✦ ✦ ✦

Later that evening, after dropping Xiaoran home, Yichen received another message from Jiao Rui.

Your girlfriend gave us a interesting perspective today.

Yichen read it, then another message appeared.

She was thoughtful, objective, and clearly understands your motivations. She didn’t exaggerate your strengths, and she was willing to acknowledge areas where you could improve.

Yichen leaned back in his car. He smiled. Then he typed.

That sounds like her.

Jiao Rui replied almost immediately.

She also seems supportive of your career.

Yichen looked through the windshield. For a moment, he thought about Xiaoran sitting in the corridor, speaking earnestly about his work ethic, his competitiveness, and his ambitions.

He imagined her explaining that she wanted him to have the chance to discover how far he could go. He had known she supported him. He had never doubted it.

But hearing that she had said it so naturally, without knowing anyone was evaluating her, made something warm settle in his chest. He typed one final message.

I’m lucky to have her.

Then he put his phone away.

✦ ✦ ✦

The next morning, Xiaoran received a message.

Yichen: Good morning.

Xiaoran: Good morning!

Yichen: I have something to tell you.

She immediately sat up in bed.

Xiaoran: WHAT

Yichen: Jiao Rui said you did well yesterday.

She stared at the screen.

Xiaoran: HE SAID THAT?

Yichen: Yes.

Xiaoran: WHAT DID HE SAY EXACTLY

Yichen: That you were thoughtful and objective.

Xiaoran: Objective???

Yichen: Apparently.

Xiaoran: I told him you’re annoying.

Yichen: He didn’t mention that part.

Xiaoran: Good.

A few seconds passed.

Xiaoran: Wait.

Xiaoran: Did you tell him I’m beautiful?

Yichen smiled at his phone.

Yichen: No.

She frowned at the screen.

Xiaoran: Why not?

Yichen: I thought that was obvious.

She stared at the message. Then her phone rang. She answered.

“What?”

“Hi.”

She tried to sound stern.

“You should have told him.”

“Told him what?”

“That I’m beautiful.”

He laughed.

“Would you like me to call him now?”

“No!”

“Why not?”

“It’s embarrassing!”

He smiled, imagining her expression.

“Yesterday you were happy to tell him I was handsome.”

“That’s different.”

“So everyone’s allowed to hear that I’m handsome, and nobody’s allowed to hear that you’re beautiful?”

“Yes! Because you already know you’re handsome!”

He laughed. Then his voice softened.

“Xiaoran.”

“Hmm?”

“Thank you for supporting me.”

She went quiet.

He said, “I know you always do. But hearing you talk about it yesterday meant a lot.”

She smiled, suddenly feeling shy.

“I didn’t say anything special.”

“You did.”

“I just told him what I thought.”

“Exactly.”

Then she said, quietly, “I really do want you to succeed.”

“I know.”

“Even if you get really busy.”

“I know.”

“Even if you have to travel.”

“I know.”

“Even if you become famous and forget your girlfriend.”

He laughed.

“That’s the one I can’t promise.”

She gasped.

“Zhou Yichen!”

He smiled.

“I’m joking.”

“You’re not funny.”

“I’m a little funny.”

“No.”

He let her complain for another moment before speaking again.

“Xiaoran.”

“What?”

“If I ever become a professional player, I think you’ll be the first person I’ll want to tell.”

She went quiet. Then she smiled.

“Then I’ll make sure my phone is always on.”

He leaned back in his chair.

“Good.”

“And I’ll come to your games.”

“I’d like that.”

“And I’ll cheer loudly.”

“I know.”

“And I’ll bring your water bottle.”

He laughed.

“Very important.”

“And if you lose, I’ll still say you’re handsome.”

He smiled.

“That’s reassuring.”

She grinned.

“See? I’m an excellent candidate.”

He shook his head, amused.

“You are.”

She didn’t know whether he meant it as a girlfriend, a supporter, or the accidental interviewee of the year. But she liked the sound of it anyway.

And Yichen, who had spent years learning to perform under pressure, compete without losing composure, and take every opportunity seriously, found himself thinking that there was something particularly wonderful about having someone who could see all of that and still remember to call him handsome.

Especially when she had no idea she was being interviewed.

chapters.desc: Her production group is filming the university team, and the captain is excellent at basketball and very bad at being filmed.
chapters.title: Her Team Films His Team
chapters.epigraph: “Winning matters. But I think how you get there matters too.”
chapters.content:
The trouble started with a camera, a production assignment, and Zhou Yichen making the mistake of agreeing to help.

Lin Xiaoran’s third-year production group had been asked to make a short promotional film for the university sports department about the basketball team getting ready for the autumn inter-university tournament. Practice footage, player interviews, behind-the-scenes moments, and a closing sequence with the captain. Xiaoran had volunteered to run the shoot. She had also made the mistake of telling her group that she knew the captain personally.

“Personally. You’ve been going out with him for four years,” Luo Jiayi had repeated.

“That’s what personally means.”

“Can you get us into training?”

“Probably.”

“Can you get us an interview?”

“Of course.”

“Can you get him to look at the camera?”

Xiaoran had paused. Then, with total confidence: “That’s easy.”

She would come to regret those words.

✦ ✦ ✦

The sports centre was already busy when she arrived with Jiayi and the others, camera strapped across her body, kit bag in one hand, clipboard under her arm. Yichen was on court warming up with the team. He saw her straight away. His face changed only slightly, not enough for anyone else to notice, but she caught the familiar easing round his eyes. He finished what he was saying to Fang Ze and came over.

“You’re early.”

“Professionals are early.”

“You’re usually late.”

“Professionals are occasionally late.”

He looked at the camera. “So you’re filming today.”

“Your team is the subject.”

“Should I be worried?”

“Only if you’ve got something to hide.”

“Nothing you don’t already know,” he said, so casually that she almost missed it.

She lifted the clipboard between them. “Go and warm up. You’re interfering with my production.”

“Yes, producer.” He bent down and kissed her cheek and jogged back to the court.

Behind her, Jiayi made a small noise.

“Why are you looking at me like that?”

“Nothing, Producer,” said Jiayi.

✦ ✦ ✦

The first twenty minutes went perfectly. The team was cooperative. Fang Ze was a natural in front of the camera and talked so much and so cheerfully that Jiayi decided at once he’d open the film. Xu Bo, the second-string guard, volunteered to demonstrate a shooting drill, missed his first shot, and insisted the camera had put him off.

“That was a warm-up shot.”

“You weren’t warming up,” said Xiaoran.

“I was warming up emotionally.”

Yichen, meanwhile, was doing everything he could to avoid being interviewed. He could play in front of a full gym. He could handle an opponent shouting in his face or a last-second shot with half the university watching. Standing in front of a camera and talking about himself was apparently another matter.

The first time she pointed it at him, he looked straight into the lens like a man facing a firing squad.

“Zhou Yichen,” she said. “Captain. Third year. What does this tournament mean to you?”

“It means we have to win.”

She waited. Jiayi waited. The camera kept running. He looked at them.

“What?”

Xiaoran lowered the camera. “That’s it?”

“That’s the answer.”

“Can you say a bit more?”

He considered it. “We’ve trained for it.”

“Yes.”

“We want to win.”

“Yes.”

“And we’ll try our best.”

Fang Ze, standing behind him, started laughing.

“What’s funny?” said Yichen, without turning round.

“Nothing, Captain.”

“Okay,” said Xiaoran. “Let’s try again.” She lifted the camera. “What makes your team different from the others this year?”

He looked into the lens. “We’re good.”

Over on the bench, Xu Bo nearly choked on his water.

Xiaoran lowered the camera slowly. “Yichen.”

“Mm.”

“You can’t just say you’re good.”

“Why not?”

“Because it’s a promotional film. You have to give people something.”

He looked genuinely thoughtful. “Then what should I say?”

It was an unfair question. He was looking at her with such calm sincerity that she honestly couldn’t tell if he was teasing.

“Talk about teamwork.”

“Teamwork is important.”

“Your preparation.”

“We prepare.”

“Your coach.”

“Our coach is good.”

Xu Bo folded in half. Fang Ze turned away. Jiayi put her hand over her mouth. Xiaoran shut her eyes.

“You’re doing this on purpose.”

“I’m answering your questions.”

“You’re answering them like you’re being interrogated.”

“Is there a difference?” he said, and the corner of his mouth went up.

“Don’t smile. I’m trying to be serious.”

That only made it worse.

✦ ✦ ✦

She changed tactics. No interview. She’d just follow him round with the camera while he worked: checking kit, talking to teammates, going through a play with the coach. Natural footage.

It turned out that Yichen became unnaturally aware of a camera the instant he noticed it. He would stop talking. Or look away. Or become fascinated by something outside the frame. At one point she was filming him and Fang Ze going through a set play, and the moment he spotted the lens his face went so blank he looked as if he were attending a disciplinary hearing.

“Keep talking!”

He kept talking. Fang Ze said something. He nodded. Then he glanced at the camera again.

She lowered it. “Why did you stop?”

“I didn’t.”

“You did.”

“I was listening.”

“You looked at me.”

“I can listen and look at you at the same time.”

“That’s actually quite romantic,” Jiayi murmured beside her.

Xiaoran elbowed her. Yichen had heard. His mouth twitched. She jerked the camera up again.

“Don’t laugh. Just keep going.”

He looked at the lens. The smile vanished. She sighed.

✦ ✦ ✦

At the break she had forty minutes of footage and almost none of it was usable. She sat on the bench by the court scrolling through it. He came and sat down next to her with a bottle of water and held it out.

“How’s the shoot?”

“Terrible.”

“Why?”

“Because someone is terrible on camera.”

“Who?”

She turned the screen towards him. He watched himself say We’re good. Then We prepare. Then a clip where he’d looked straight into the lens and said absolutely nothing for six seconds before asking whether she was finished. His face didn’t change at all.

“Well?” she said.

“It seems fine.”

“Fine? You look like you’re being held hostage.”

He laughed. “That’s an exaggeration.”

“You’re smiling right now. In real life. Why can’t you do that when it’s on?”

“Because you’re behind it.”

“What does that mean?”

He drank some water. “When you’re talking to me, I’m looking at you. When you point that at me, I’m looking at the camera. And then I don’t know where to look.”

She stared at him. Then she laughed out loud. “You’re the captain. You’ve played in front of thousands of people.”

“That’s different. They’re watching the game.”

“We’re filming you playing the game!”

“That’s also different.”

“You’re hopeless,” she said, and tucked herself against his shoulder.

He put his cheek against her hair. “Do you want me to try again?”

She lifted her head. “Yes.”

“All right.”

“Really?”

“Of course. You’re welcome, Producer.” He tipped her chin up with one finger.

✦ ✦ ✦

She set him up by the court, in front of the university banner. Good light, clean background, the rest of the team banished out of shot. She checked the framing and then stepped out from behind the camera and stood just to the side of the lens.

“Okay. Don’t look at the camera. Look at me.”

“Not the camera?”

“Not yet. Just me.”

He met her eyes.

“Tell me about your team.”

And it was as if he’d forgotten the camera existed.

He said, “We’ve been together a long time. Most of us have played with each other for two or three seasons. We know each other’s habits. What everyone’s good at, what they’re not. When somebody needs pushing, and when they need room. It’s been a hard season. People have been injured. Some of us have had to fit training round internships. We’ve had to change how we play more than once. But everyone kept turning up. That’s what I’m proud of. Not the results. The way everyone kept turning up.”

Xiaoran smiled. “Good.”

He nodded, and looked at the camera, and his face shut like a door.

“Don’t look at it yet!”

“Sorry.”

“One more. Imagine you’re talking to someone who knows nothing about basketball. Why should they come and watch?”

He thought about it, looking at her. “Because it’s better in person. You can hear us talking to each other on court. You can see how fast things change. And you can tell how much work goes into every single possession. Would you come?”

She blinked. “To the tournament?”

“Yes.”

“I’m already coming.”

“I know.”

“Then why are you asking?”

“Just checking,” he said, and she looked down hard at her clipboard.

Behind the camera Jiayi whispered, “That one’s usable.”

Xiaoran pretended not to hear.

✦ ✦ ✦

After that it got better, because she stopped trying to make him perform. She filmed him in drills, caught him laughing at something Fang Ze said, recorded him explaining a defensive rotation to a first-year, got him walking off court with a towel round his neck. Those were the moments he looked most like himself.

During a shooting drill she filmed him make five in a row. The sixth bounced off the rim. He caught the rebound and looked straight at her.

She lowered the camera. “What?”

“I missed.”

“You’re allowed to miss.”

“Not when you’re filming.”

“Don’t worry. I’ll cut it.”

“You’re going to edit out my mistakes?”

“Of course.”

“That’s dishonest.”

“That’s filmmaking,” she said, and he laughed and passed the ball to Fang Ze.

Later, going through the footage, she noticed he’d made every single shot she’d filmed all afternoon, except that sixth one. She kept it.

✦ ✦ ✦

The closing statement was last. She set the camera up one more time. He stood in front of it in his training shirt with his hair damp and his face still flushed from the drills.

“Okay. Last one. When the tournament’s over, what do you want people to remember about this team?”

He looked at her. Then at the camera. Then back at her. She smiled at him. He took a breath.

“I hope they remember we played together. That we trusted each other even when it wasn’t going well. That we didn’t stop working when the result wasn’t what we wanted. Winning matters. But I think how you get there matters too.”

For once, he hadn’t looked away from the lens at all.

“Good,” she said.

He nodded. Then, just as she reached to stop recording: “Are you finished?”

She burst out laughing. “Yes!”

His whole body relaxed. “Good.”

“You’re so bad at this.”

“But you got what you needed,” he said, and she looked at the screen, and he was right.

✦ ✦ ✦

Two days later she was editing at her desk in her studio with her headphones on and notes everywhere. He was on her sofa with a case study for his strategy module. Every so often he looked over. She’d been quiet for nearly an hour. Then she made a small sound.

He waited. She played something again. Then she started laughing helplessly.

He put his book down. “What?”

She patted the space beside her.

He came and stood behind her chair, and she turned the laptop so he could see. On the screen, Zhou Yichen, shoulders squared, hands clasped, looked directly into the lens and said in a completely serious voice, “We’re good.”

Xiaoran laughed until she nearly fell off the chair.

“Why are you watching that?”

“Because it’s funny.”

“It’s a perfectly normal answer.”

“It’s not.” She clicked. We prepare. Clicked. Our coach is good.

He shut his eyes. “Xiaoran.”

She couldn’t answer. She was crying with laughter.

“You’re keeping those?”

“Absolutely.”

“For what?”

“Personal archive.”

“Delete them.”

“No.”

“Producer.”

“Captain.”

“Delete them.”

She swivelled the chair round to face him. “Are you embarrassed?”

“No.”

“Then why should I delete them?”

He looked at her with a slow smile. “Because I know you. You’ll send them to Meilin.”

Her grin widened. She had already sent one to Meilin.

He sighed. “Of course.”

✦ ✦ ✦

They submitted it the next afternoon. Four minutes and ten seconds: the warm-up, the drills, the interviews, Fang Ze’s opening, and Yichen’s closing statement. The sports department approved it in an hour and asked if they could put it on the university’s official account.

Meilin: I watched the video

Xiaoran: good right??

Meilin: very professional. your boyfriend looks handsome

Xiaoran: obviously

Meilin: but why does he look like he’s at a job interview

Xiaoran: don’t start

Meilin: the bit where he says “we’re good” is my favourite

Xiaoran: that’s not in the final cut

Meilin: tragic. it’s his best work

That evening she brought the laptop over to the sofa and played him the final version, curled up against his side with her legs over his. He watched all of it. This time he didn’t complain once. When it ended, he nodded.

“Good work.”

She shut the laptop. “You’re actually good on camera. When you’re not trying.”

“Is that a compliment?”

“Yes. I think I know why you’re so bad at it. When you’re playing, you don’t care who’s watching. You’re just playing. When you’re talking to the team, you’re just talking. But the second you know the camera’s there, you start thinking about how you look.” She let her head drop onto his shoulder.

“That’s quite an analysis.”

“I’m a media student.”

“Of course you are.”

“And maybe you’re just not used to being the subject. Do you know what I liked most?” She looked up at him.

“What?”

“When you forgot I was filming. That’s when you looked most like you.”

He was quiet. Then he brushed her hair back from her cheek. “You’re very good at this.”

“At filming?”

“At noticing things.”

“I know,” she said, pleased, and he laughed, and she kissed him.

When she tried to sit up he caught her hand. “One condition. Next time you film me, no interviews. Just film the game.”

“That’s not a bad idea.”

“Good.”

“But I might still ask you one question.”

He looked at her with deep suspicion. “What question?”

She leaned in close and smiled at him sweetly. “Zhou Yichen. Why are you so handsome?”

He stared at her. Then the slow smile came. “Is that for your assignment?”

She went pink. “No.”

“Then you don’t need the camera,” he said, and pulled her down and kissed her.

chapters.desc: His first professional scrimmage, and his name isn’t called. Somebody’s father made a phone call.
chapters.title: The First Time He Doesn’t Play
chapters.epigraph: “Then keep trying.”
chapters.content:
The first time Zhou Yichen sat on the sidelines of a professional basketball court, he wasn’t injured. He wasn’t resting.

And he hadn’t been told to conserve his energy. He simply hadn’t been selected. It was a strange feeling.

For the past several weeks, he had been working towards this opportunity. He had passed the initial evaluation, impressed the coaching staff enough to be invited back, and earned a place in the extended training group.

He knew he wasn’t the strongest player there. He wasn’t naive enough to believe that one good evaluation would make him indispensable. He was prepared to compete. He was prepared to be challenged.

What he hadn’t expected was to be excluded before the competition even began. The morning started normally.

He arrived early, changed into his training uniform, and joined the other players for warm-ups. He greeted the coaching staff, exchanged a few words with the players he had met during the previous evaluation, and began stretching. Then the head coach announced the scrimmage lineup. Names were called. One by one, players moved towards the court. Yichen waited. His name never came.

At first, he assumed there would be another rotation, then the assistant coach approached him.

“Zhou Yichen?”

“Yes.”

“You’ll observe this session from the sidelines.”

Yichen glanced towards the court.

“Am I injured?”

“No. The coaching staff has made the selection for today’s scrimmage.”

He nodded once.

“Understood.”

The assistant coach seemed ready to leave, but Yichen asked one more question.

“Is there anything specific you’d like me to observe?”

The man paused.

“Just watch the session.”

Yichen nodded.

“Okay.”

And that was it. No explanation. No criticism. No feedback.

He picked up his water bottle and moved towards the bench.

✦ ✦ ✦

Xiaoran noticed something was wrong almost immediately. She had arrived a little later than usual because Yichen had told her the session would start with a warm-up and that she didn’t need to rush.

She entered the spectator area carrying two drinks and scanned the court. She found him. But he wasn’t playing.

He was sitting on the bench, elbows resting on his knees, watching the scrimmage.

For a moment, she thought he might be waiting for his turn.

She sat down and placed his drink beside him.

“Yichen.”

“Hey.”

“Why are you sitting here?”

“Not selected for the scrimmage.”

Her smile faded slightly.

“Oh.”

He reached for the bottle.

“It’s fine.”

She watched him open it.

“Are you injured?”

“No.”

“Did something happen?”

“No.”

He took a drink.

“They selected a different group.”

She looked towards the court. Several players were moving through a fast-paced drill. One of them was a young man she vaguely recognised from the previous evaluation.

“Are you going to play later?”

“Not sure.”

She nodded slowly. Then she looked at him again. He seemed perfectly calm.

His posture was relaxed. His expression was neutral. He wasn’t visibly upset or embarrassed.

But Xiaoran knew him well enough to recognise when his quietness meant something. She sat beside him.

“Do you want me to stay?”

He glanced at her.

“You came all this way. Of course you can stay.”

She smiled faintly.

“That’s not what I asked.”

He looked at her for a second. Then he reached over and touched her hand.

“Stay if you want to.”

So she stayed. For the next three hours, Yichen didn’t play a single minute. He watched the scrimmage from beginning to end. At first, Xiaoran tried to watch with him.

She followed the ball, paid attention to the players, and occasionally glanced at Yichen to see whether he was taking notes. He was. Not on paper, but mentally.

He watched how the guards communicated. He observed the defensive rotations, the pace of transitions, and the way certain players created space.

He wasn’t simply sitting there waiting to be called. He was studying.

But after a while, Xiaoran began noticing something that bothered her.

A player on the court was making repeated mistakes.

He missed an open pass. He lost possession twice. He failed to rotate during a defensive play, leaving another player to cover his position. Yet he remained in the scrimmage. The coaches didn’t remove him. Instead, they seemed unusually patient with him.

During a break, the player walked towards the coaching staff. One of the men approached him, placed a hand on his shoulder, and spoke to him with a familiarity that didn’t resemble the way the other players were being treated. Xiaoran leaned slightly towards Yichen.

“Who’s that?”

“Which one?”

“The one wearing number seventeen.”

Yichen glanced over.

“Not sure. I think his family knows someone in management.”

She frowned.

“Does he play well?”

Yichen looked back at the court.

“He has potential.”

It was a careful answer. Xiaoran looked at him.

“That’s not what I asked.”

He smiled faintly.

“Then no. Not particularly well today.”

She looked back at the player.

“Then why is he still playing?”

Yichen didn’t answer immediately. He watched the player receive the ball, attempt a difficult shot, and miss. A teammate retrieved the rebound. The scrimmage continued.

“Maybe the coaches see something I don’t,” he said.

Xiaoran didn’t look convinced.

✦ ✦ ✦

The explanation came during lunch. Yichen had stepped away to speak with one of the assistant coaches. Xiaoran was sitting alone near the cafeteria entrance when she overheard two staff members talking. They weren’t speaking particularly.

“Wasn’t that the director’s nephew?”

“That’s what I heard.”

“His father called this morning. Apparently, they want him included in the development group.”

“And Zhou?”

“Which one?”

“The university player. Yichen.”

“Oh. He’s good, but the decision has already been made for today’s session.”

“That’s unfortunate. His evaluation numbers were better.”

One of them gave a small laugh.

“Numbers aren’t everything.”

The conversation moved on. Xiaoran sat still. She looked through the glass towards the training court.

Yichen was standing beside the assistant coach, listening to something being explained. His expression was attentive. He nodded. Asked a question, then thanked the coach.

He looked completely unaware of what she had just heard. Or perhaps he already knew.

She wasn’t sure which possibility made her feel worse. She waited until they were alone.

They were walking towards the parking area when she finally spoke.

“Yichen.”

“Hmm?”

“I heard something.”

He looked at her.

“What?”

She hesitated.

“About number seventeen.”

His expression changed slightly. Then he looked ahead again.

“What about him?”

“Apparently, he’s related to someone in management.”

Yichen didn’t respond. She continued.

“Someone said he was included because his family asked for it.”

He adjusted the strap of his bag.

“That’s possible.”

“Possible?”

He nodded.

“I don’t know the full situation.”

She stopped walking. He took another step before noticing.

When he turned, she was looking at him with a deeply unhappy expression.

“What’s wrong?”

“You knew?”

He considered the question.

“I suspected.”

“Since when?”

“After the lineup was announced.”

She stared at him.

“Then why didn’t you tell me?”

He walked back towards her.

“Because I didn’t have anything confirmed.”

“But you knew something was wrong.”

“I knew I hadn’t been selected. That’s all.”

“Yichen.”

He looked at her. She seemed to be struggling with something. It wasn’t quite anger. It was more complicated than that.

“Did they even give you a chance?”

He was quiet. Then he answered honestly.

“Not today.”

Her eyes became glossy. He noticed immediately.

“Hey.”

She looked away.

“I’m fine.”

“Xiaoran.”

“I’m not the one who sat on a bench for three hours.”

He let out a small breath. He held out his hand. She didn’t move.

He reached for her hand and gently pulled her closer. She looked up at him.

“I hate it.”

“I know.”

“I hate that you worked so hard, and then someone can just decide that another person should get your place.”

He listened.

“I know you’re not supposed to be selected every time. I know you still have to prove yourself. But you should at least be given the chance to play.”

Her voice grew quieter.

“You went there to compete.”

He looked at her. Then he lifted his hand and brushed his thumb over her cheek.

“I know.”

“Doesn’t it make you angry?”

He didn’t answer immediately. Then he said, “Yes.”

She looked at him. It was the first time he had admitted it.

“I am angry. But I’m not going to let that become the only thing I take away from today,” he said.

She lowered her eyes. He gently tilted her chin back towards him.

“I watched the entire scrimmage. I learned how they rotate, how they defend, and what kind of pace they expect. I also saw what I need to improve.”

“But you should have been playing.”

“Maybe.”

“Yichen…”

He smiled faintly.

“I’m not saying it doesn’t matter.”

He took her hand.

“I’m saying I don’t want to spend the rest of the day thinking about someone else’s connections.”

He said, “I came here because I want to become a better player. I still want that.”

Her expression softened.

✦ ✦ ✦

That evening, Yichen was unusually quiet. He finished dinner, showered, and sat at his desk reviewing the footage he had managed to obtain from the session.

Xiaoran was on his bed, lying on her stomach and watching him. She had been quiet for nearly twenty minutes. Eventually, she couldn’t take it anymore.

“Yichen.”

“Hmm?”

She held out her hand. He turned his chair.

“What?”

“Hug first.”

He looked at her, then closed his laptop. She moved towards the edge of the bed. He stood and walked over.

“What is it?”

She held out both hands. He took them. Then she pulled him down until he was sitting beside her.

“Are you disappointed?”

He looked at her. She looked back. He knew she wasn’t asking whether he was angry. She wanted to know whether he was hurt. And perhaps he was.

A little more than he had allowed himself to acknowledge.

“I am,” he admitted.

Her fingers tightened around his.

“I thought I would get to play today. I prepared for it.”

She nodded.

“I know.”

“I wanted to see how I performed against them. I wanted to know where I stood.”

He looked down at their hands.

“Instead, I spent the afternoon watching.”

Xiaoran moved closer.

“I’m sorry.”

“Why are you apologising?”

“Because I don’t know what else to say.”

He smiled slightly.

“You don’t have to say anything.”

She shook her head.

“I want to.”

Then she leaned forward and wrapped her arms around him.

He accepted the hug, one hand settling against her back. She pressed her cheek against his shoulder.

“You know what I think?”

“What?”

“I think they made a mistake.”

He laughed.

“That’s a little biased.”

“I’m allowed to be biased.”

“Of course.”

She pulled back.

“But I also think you’re going to prove yourself. Not because you need to prove anything to that person. Just because I know how much you love playing.”

He looked at her. She touched his cheek.

“I like watching you play, Yichen.”

His expression softened.

“Even when I don’t win?”

“Even then.”

He raised an eyebrow.

“Meaning?”

“Because you look very serious when you’re trying to fix them.”

He laughed. She smiled. Then her expression became gentle again.

“I don’t want you to think that today means you’re not good enough.”

She said, “You were invited there for a reason. They saw something in you. One person’s decision doesn’t erase that.”

He looked at her. Then he leaned forward and kissed her temple.

“Thank you.”

She smiled.

“Welcome.”

He kissed her cheek, then the other. She narrowed her eyes.

“Why are you kissing me?”

“Am I not allowed?”

“You’re distracting me.”

“Good.”

She laughed and leaned into him.

✦ ✦ ✦

The following morning, Yichen arrived at the training facility earlier than usual.

He greeted the staff, changed, and began his warm-up.

He didn’t know whether he would be selected for the next scrimmage.

He didn’t know whether the same situation would happen again. But he came prepared. During the individual drills, he performed well.

His footwork was sharper. His passes were more deliberate. His defensive positioning had improved. He listened to the coaches. He corrected mistakes. He worked.

At the end of the session, the assistant coach approached him.

“Zhou Yichen.”

He turned.

“Yes?”

“Good work today.”

“Thank you.”

“The head coach would like to see you tomorrow. There may be another opportunity for you to join the scrimmage.”

Yichen nodded.

“Understood.”

The assistant coach paused.

“Don’t be discouraged by yesterday.”

Yichen looked at him.

The man continued, “There are decisions happening here that aren’t always related to performance. You should know that.”

For the first time, Yichen’s expression became slightly colder.

“I understand.”

“Keep doing what you’re doing.”

“I will.”

The assistant coach left. Yichen stood there. Then he picked up his bag. He didn’t feel triumphant. He wasn’t reassured. But he felt something settle inside him. At least someone had acknowledged it. Xiaoran was waiting outside when he came out. She was holding two drinks again. He smiled when he saw her.

“Again?”

“It’s becoming my job.”

“Should I pay you?”

She considered it.

“Maybe.”

He took the drink.

“How was today?”

“Good.”

“Really?”

“Mm.”

She looked at his face, trying to read it.

Then he told her about the assistant coach’s conversation. She listened carefully. When he finished, she nodded.

“Good.”

“That’s all?”

She looked at him.

“What else should I say?”

“Perhaps something about how handsome I was during practice.”

She stared at him, then burst out laughing.

“Zhou Yichen!”

“Was I not?”

She shook her head, still laughing.

“Unbelievable.”

He reached for her hand.

“Let’s go.”

She walked beside him, swinging their joined hands lightly. She looked up.

“Yichen?”

“Hmm?”

“Next time you play, I’ll cheer louder.”

He glanced at her.

“Were you holding back?”

“Very.”

“That’s unfortunate.”

She smiled.

“I’m saving it.”

He squeezed her hand.

“Then I’ll look forward to it.”

✦ ✦ ✦

The next day, Yichen was selected for the development group’s scrimmage. Not because someone had decided to be generous.

Not because the club had changed its mind about nepotism.

He was selected because the coaching staff wanted to evaluate him properly. And this time, he played.

He didn’t dominate every possession. He made mistakes, missed a shot, and had to adjust to the pace of players who were more experienced than he was. But he competed. He defended. He communicated.

He made a difficult pass that created an opening for his teammate, and later scored from a position he had been studying since the previous session. From the spectator area, Xiaoran finally stood up.

“YES!”

Several people turned. She immediately sat down. Yichen heard her anyway. He glanced towards the seats. She gave him an enthusiastic thumbs-up.

He smiled briefly before returning his attention to the game. After the session, he walked towards her. She was already waiting.

“How was I?”

He raised an eyebrow.

“That’s your question?”

“Yes.”

He pretended to think.

“Not bad.”

She gasped.

“Not bad?”

He smiled.

“Pretty good.”

“Yichen!”

He laughed and pulled her into a hug. She wrapped her arms around his waist.

“I saw everything.”

“Did you?”

“Yes. Your pass was amazing.”

“Thank you.”

“And your defence.”

“Mm.”

“And that shot.”

He smiled.

“You watched carefully.”

“Of course.”

She looked up at him.

“I’m glad you got to play.”

His expression softened.

“Me too.”

She reached up and gently wiped a small drop of sweat near his temple.

Then she said, “You know, the day you sat on the bench, I was very angry.”

“I noticed.”

“Today I’m happy.”

“I’m glad.”

“But I’m still angry.”

He laughed.

“That’s fair.”

She smiled. He bent and kissed her hairline.

Then he whispered, “I think I’ll remember that day for a long time.”

She looked at him.

“Because you didn’t play?”

“Because I learned something.”

“What?”

He glanced towards the court.

“That getting an opportunity doesn’t always mean getting a fair chance.”

She listened.

“But it also doesn’t mean I should stop trying.”

He looked back at her.

“And I think I needed to learn that.”

She smiled. Then she caught his face in both hands and kissed his cheek.

“Then keep trying.”

He held her hand.

“I will.”

And they left the training facility together. His phone buzzed on the way to the car. The schedule for Friday: the third evaluation, a full scrimmage, groups to be confirmed on the day.

He showed her the screen. She read it twice and looked up at him with her eyes bright.

“Friday,” she said.

“Friday.”

“I’m coming.”

He had known that before she said it.

chapters.desc: The third evaluation, the main group at last, and a folder of letters from people who never told him they’d written.
chapters.title: The Player They Almost Overlooked
chapters.epigraph: “I liked that you didn’t let them make you feel small.”
chapters.content:
Zhou Yichen had never been particularly interested in being underestimated.

He didn’t enjoy proving people wrong for the sake of it. He didn’t need an audience to work hard, and he certainly wasn’t the type to turn every disagreement into a competition. But he did believe in one thing.

If someone wanted to judge his ability, they should at least give him the chance to play.

He had spent three hours on a bench while another player’s family connections bought a place in the scrimmage. He had played two days later, and played well, but one good afternoon with the development group hadn’t answered the question the bench had left him with: whether the club was genuinely interested in his ability at all.

Fortunately, he wasn’t the only person who had noticed. The third evaluation was scheduled for Friday morning. Xiaoran accompanied him, as usual.

She had become familiar with the training facility by now. She knew which entrance led to the spectator area, which vending machine occasionally swallowed coins, and which staff member always greeted Yichen by name.

She also knew that Yichen had been training harder than usual. He hadn’t complained. He hadn’t mentioned the previous incident again.

But she had seen him reviewing footage late at night, practising his footwork after university training, and adjusting his schedule to accommodate the additional sessions.

She had also noticed that he was quieter whenever the club contacted him.

That morning, she found him adjusting the straps of his sports bag.

“Ready?”

“Almost.”

She looked at him.

“Nervous?”

“A little.”

She smiled.

“Good.”

He raised an eyebrow.

“Good?”

“Means you care.”

He laughed. Then he pressed a kiss to her hair.

“Stay hydrated.”

“I’m not the one playing.”

“You forget to drink water when you’re watching.”

She gasped.

“That’s not true.”

He gave her a look. She took the water bottle from him.

“Fine.”

“Good girl.”

She immediately looked away.

“Don’t say that in public.”

He laughed and took her hand.

✦ ✦ ✦

The atmosphere inside the training facility was noticeably different.

There were more people present than during the previous sessions.

Two senior coaches stood near the court, speaking with a man Xiaoran recognised from the first evaluation. A few staff members were carrying tablets and clipboards. Near the entrance, a woman in a dark blazer was reviewing a printed document with the club’s general manager. Yichen greeted the staff he knew. One of the assistant coaches approached him.

“Zhou. Good to see you.”

“Good morning.”

“Ready for today?”

“Yes.”

The coach smiled.

“Good. We’ll be running a full scrimmage.”

Yichen nodded.

Then the coach added, “You’ll be playing with the main group.”

For a brief moment, Yichen’s expression changed. Not dramatically. Just enough for Xiaoran to notice.

“Understood. Thank you.”

The assistant coach patted his shoulder before walking away. Xiaoran waited until they were alone.

“Main group?”

“That’s what he said.”

She smiled.

“Finally.”

Yichen looked at her.

“Don’t get too excited.”

“I’m already excited.”

“Try not to shout.”

“No promises.”

He laughed and went to change.

✦ ✦ ✦

The scrimmage began twenty minutes later. Yichen was assigned to the second unit, playing alongside several experienced players. It wasn’t an easy position.

He was the newest member of the group, and the others had already developed an understanding of one another. Their movements were instinctive. They knew when to cut, when to pass, and when to switch defensive assignments without needing to communicate. Yichen had to read them quickly. The first few minutes were cautious.

He focused on positioning, made simple passes, and avoided forcing opportunities that weren’t there, then the pace increased.

An opposing guard attempted to drive through the middle.

Yichen anticipated the movement and shifted across, forcing him towards the sideline. The player passed the ball away, but Yichen had already moved to cover the next passing lane. The ball changed possession. His teammate looked towards him.

Yichen received the pass, assessed the court, and immediately sent it to the opposite wing. A clean shot. Three points. The head coach looked up from his notes. A few possessions later, Yichen was tested again.

This time, his defender was taller and more physically experienced. He attempted to use his strength to push Yichen away from the basket. Yichen held his position. He didn’t try to overpower him.

Instead, he adjusted his angle, anticipated the next movement, and forced a difficult shot. Miss. Rebound. His team recovered the ball. The scrimmage continued.

From the spectator area, Xiaoran had stopped looking at her phone entirely.

She was leaning forward, both hands wrapped around her drink.

She wasn’t familiar with every technical detail, but she understood enough to recognise the difference between Yichen playing well and Yichen being challenged. Today, he was being challenged. And he was responding. Halfway through the session, something happened.

One of the senior players made a mistake during a defensive rotation. The opposing team immediately exploited the opening, creating a clear scoring opportunity. Yichen saw it.

He moved across the court, covered the gap, and prevented the shot. But the recovery left his own position exposed. The ball moved again. A teammate shouted for help.

Yichen turned, sprinted back, and managed to contest the shot just before it was released. The ball bounced off the rim. His teammate collected it. The coach blew his whistle.

“Good recovery!”

Yichen nodded and returned to position. He didn’t celebrate. He simply continued playing.

At the sideline, one of the evaluators leaned towards the head coach.

“That’s the university player?”

“Yes. Zhou Yichen.”

“He reads the court well.”

“Very well. His defensive awareness has improved considerably since the initial recommendation.”

The evaluator watched another possession.

“He’s not forcing his way into the game.”

“No. That’s one of his better qualities.”

The head coach glanced at his notes.

“He’s adaptable. We received his university performance reports before the first evaluation. His coaches have been quite consistent in their assessment.”

The evaluator looked down at the document.

“Three separate recommendations?”

“Three.”

He nodded.

“Interesting.”

The first half ended. Yichen walked towards the bench, breathing heavily. A teammate passed him a towel.

“Good defence.”

“Thanks.”

“You’re from the university team?”

“Yeah.”

“Which university?”

Yichen told him. The player nodded.

“Your coach is quite well known. I think our assistant coach trained with him years ago.”

Yichen smiled politely.

“Possibly.”

Before the conversation could continue, the assistant coach approached.

“Zhou, take a few minutes. We’ll rotate the lineup.”

Yichen nodded. He sat down and drank water. Then his phone vibrated.

Xiaoran: You’re doing so well.

He glanced towards the spectator area. She was already smiling at him.

Yichen: Watch the game.

Xiaoran: I am watching.

Yichen: Then stop texting.

Xiaoran: You’re very bossy.

He smiled and put his phone away.

✦ ✦ ✦

The second half was more demanding. The coaches changed the matchups, placing Yichen against one of the strongest guards in the group. It was a deliberate challenge.

The player was fast, physically strong, and experienced enough to recognise defensive patterns. For the first few possessions, Yichen struggled. His opponent got past him once and scored. Then he drew a foul. Yichen didn’t react. He adjusted his stance and watched more carefully.

The next time, he forced the player towards the left side. The possession became uncomfortable.

The opponent tried to create space, but Yichen stayed close enough to contest the shot without committing a foul. The shot missed. On the next possession, Yichen intercepted a pass.

He moved forward, but instead of attempting to score himself, he passed to a teammate who had a better angle. The teammate scored. The head coach nodded.

A few minutes later, Yichen made his own shot, then another.

He wasn’t suddenly the best player on the court. He wasn’t dominating the scrimmage.

But he was making himself useful in ways that mattered. He was learning the rhythm of the team. He was communicating. He was defending. He was making decisions under pressure.

And most importantly, he wasn’t trying to prove that he deserved to be there by doing everything himself. He was playing basketball.

By the final whistle, the sweat had soaked through his training shirt.

He bent forward with his hands on his knees, catching his breath. The assistant coach approached.

“Good session.”

“Thank you.”

“Get some water. We’ll speak afterward.”

Yichen nodded. Across the court, the head coach was already speaking with the evaluators. One of them was smiling.

✦ ✦ ✦

Xiaoran was waiting outside the changing area when Yichen came out.

He had showered and changed into a clean shirt, his sports bag hanging over one shoulder. She immediately approached him.

“Yichen!”

“Hello.”

“You were amazing.”

She reached for his hand.

“I saw everything.”

“Everything?”

“Almost everything.”

He raised an eyebrow. She corrected herself.

“Most of everything.”

He laughed. Then she looked at him more carefully.

“Are you happy?”

He considered it.

“Yes.”

She smiled.

“Good.”

He brushed his thumb over her knuckles.

“Let’s wait a little. Coach said he wanted to speak with me.”

They sat near the corridor. Xiaoran leaned against his shoulder, occasionally glancing towards the meeting room. A few minutes later, the door opened.

The head coach came out with two senior staff members.

“Zhou Yichen?”

Yichen stood.

“Yes.”

“Come with us for a moment.”

He nodded, then the head coach glanced at Xiaoran.

“Your girlfriend can join us if she’d like. We won’t be discussing anything confidential.”

Xiaoran looked surprised. Yichen turned towards her.

“Come.”

She stood immediately. The meeting room was smaller than she expected.

There was a long table, several chairs, and a screen displaying footage from the scrimmage.

Lou Wei, the scout from the back of the university gym, was there, along with the head coach and another senior evaluator.

A woman introduced herself as the club’s recruitment director.

“Zhou, please sit.”

Yichen took the seat nearest the screen. Xiaoran sat beside him. The recruitment director opened a folder.

“First, I want to say that today’s performance was very encouraging.”

Yichen nodded.

“Thank you.”

“We’ve reviewed your initial evaluation, your second assessment, and today’s scrimmage. There are several areas we’d like you to continue developing, but your overall progress has been quite consistent.”

She turned towards the screen.

“This is one of the plays from the second half.”

The footage showed Yichen defending against the senior guard.

“Your opponent had a physical advantage. You didn’t attempt to match his strength directly. Instead, you changed your positioning and restricted his options.”

She paused the video.

“That was a good decision.”

Yichen watched the screen.

“I thought he would try to drive towards the middle again.”

“And you anticipated it correctly.”

The head coach leaned back.

“Your university coach mentioned that you tend to learn quickly from repeated situations. We saw that today.”

Yichen nodded.

“I’m glad.”

The recruitment director looked through her notes.

“We’ve also received additional information from your university.”

Yichen looked up.

“Additional information?”

“Yes.”

She placed several documents on the table.

“Your head coach submitted a formal recommendation after your first evaluation. We also received an endorsement from the university’s Director of Athletics.”

Yichen glanced at the documents. The university’s official letterhead was visible. The recruitment director continued.

“Your department’s faculty advisor also provided confirmation of your academic standing and your ability to manage your university responsibilities alongside competitive training.”

Xiaoran looked at Yichen. He seemed genuinely surprised. The director smiled.

“Apparently, you have quite a few people supporting you.”

Yichen looked down at the documents again.

“May I ask who submitted the recommendation?”

“Certainly.”

She opened the folder.

“Your university head coach, naturally. The Director of Athletics, who oversees the university’s competitive sports programs. The university’s Sports Development Office also provided your competition records and training history.”

She paused.

“And Professor Xie, your faculty’s academic advisor, sent a separate letter confirming that you’ve maintained good academic performance while participating in the basketball program.”

Yichen blinked. Professor Xie? He knew the professor. He had never discussed the professional trial with him in detail. The recruitment director continued.

“Your university’s Deputy Director of Student Affairs also contacted our club through an official university channel. He didn’t ask us to select you. He simply wanted to ensure that your application was considered properly and that your academic and athletic commitments were understood.”

Yichen looked at her.

“Why would he do that?”

The head coach answered.

“Because your university takes its athletes seriously.”

He smiled.

“Your university coach has been recommending you for some time. He believes you have the discipline and potential to progress beyond university-level competition. The Director of Athletics agreed.”

The recruitment director added, “They were particularly clear about one thing. They wanted you evaluated on your own performance.”

Yichen was quiet. He hadn’t expected this. He knew his university coach thought highly of him. He knew the basketball department had been supportive.

But he hadn’t realised that several people had taken the time to formally advocate for him. The head coach leaned forward.

“There’s something else you should know.”

Yichen looked at him.

“The first scrimmage.”

The room became a little quieter. The recruitment director exchanged a glance with the head coach.

“We’re aware that you weren’t selected.”

Yichen nodded.

“Yes.”

“We also know that the selection process for that particular session was influenced by an external recommendation.”

Xiaoran’s expression changed. The head coach continued.

“One of the players included in that lineup had a family connection to a senior figure associated with the club. His participation was requested.”

Yichen remained still. The recruitment director spoke more directly.

“To be clear, that decision was not made by the technical evaluation team. It was an administrative request that affected the initial lineup.”

Xiaoran looked at Yichen. He didn’t appear surprised. But his jaw had tightened slightly. The head coach continued.

“We reviewed the situation internally. The player in question has his own development pathway, and we don’t object to giving young athletes opportunities. But opportunities in a professional environment must still be supported by performance.”

He looked directly at Yichen.

“You were invited because our scouts saw potential in you. You should have been given a proper opportunity to demonstrate it from the beginning.”

Yichen nodded once.

“Thank you for clarifying.”

The recruitment director closed the folder.

“We don’t want you to think that today’s session was arranged to compensate for what happened previously.”

Yichen looked at her.

“Today’s evaluation was conducted because we wanted to assess you properly. The technical staff were satisfied with your performance, and the results were consistent with the recommendations we received.”

“Your university has been very supportive, but the final decision will still depend on our own assessment.”

Yichen nodded.

“I understand.”

“Good.”

The head coach looked at him.

“We’d like to invite you to the next stage.”

For the first time during the meeting, Yichen’s expression visibly changed.

“The next stage?”

“Yes. A longer training period with the development group. You’ll train with us on selected days, and we’ll continue assessing your performance, physical condition, and compatibility with the team.”

The recruitment director added, “It’s not a contract offer yet. But it’s a meaningful step.”

Yichen sat a little straighter.

“Thank you. I’d be very interested.”

The head coach smiled.

“We thought you might be.”

Xiaoran had been quiet throughout the meeting. She was trying to behave. She really was.

But when the meeting ended and they stepped into the corridor, she immediately turned towards Yichen.

“Yichen.”

He looked down.

“Hmm?”

“Your university.”

He smiled.

“What about it?”

“They did all that?”

“Apparently.”

She looked almost overwhelmed.

“Your head coach, the athletic director, your professor…”

“And the student affairs office.”

She stared at him.

“That’s so many people.”

He laughed.

“I didn’t know either.”

She looked at him for another moment. Then her expression changed.

“Wait.”

“What?”

“Your professor actually wrote a letter?”

“Looks like it.”

“Professor Xie?”

“Mm.”

“The one who always asks you why you’re leaving class early for training?”

He laughed.

“Yes.”

She covered her mouth.

“He likes you!”

“He’s my professor.”

“He likes you as a student!”

“That’s generally how it works.”

She ignored him. Then she looked at the meeting room again.

“Yichen, they really believe in you.”

He followed her gaze. He didn’t say anything. Then he nodded.

“Yes.”

Her smile became softer.

“That’s nice.”

“Very.”

She reached for his hand. He took it. And they continued walking.

✦ ✦ ✦

The confrontation happened unexpectedly. They were passing the reception area when a familiar voice called out.

“Zhou Yichen.”

Yichen turned. It was the man from the club’s administration office who had handled the initial lineup arrangements.

Beside him stood the young player from the first scrimmage. Number seventeen. He looked uncomfortable. The staff member approached.

“I heard you’ve been invited to the next stage.”

“Yes.”

“Congratulations.”

“Thank you.”

There was an awkward pause.

Then the staff member said, “About the first session…”

Yichen waited.

“I understand that the situation may have been frustrating.”

Xiaoran glanced at Yichen.

The staff member continued, “The club sometimes receives requests from people who have supported the organisation for a long time. It’s not always easy to manage those expectations.”

Yichen’s expression remained calm.

“I understand that.”

The man seemed relieved.

“Good. I hope there are no hard feelings.”

Yichen looked at him. Then he answered, politely but clearly.

“I don’t have a problem with someone being given an opportunity.”

The staff member nodded.

“But I do think everyone should understand what that opportunity means.”

The man’s expression changed slightly. Yichen continued.

“If a player is selected for a scrimmage, I assume it’s because the technical staff want to evaluate his ability. If the selection is made for another reason, that’s fine too. But it shouldn’t be confused with a professional assessment.”

The corridor became quiet. The young player looked down. Yichen didn’t raise his voice. He didn’t sound angry.

If anything, his composure made his words more difficult to dismiss.

“I came here because I was invited to compete. I prepared for the sessions, and I expected to be evaluated on the court. That’s all.”

The staff member cleared his throat.

“Of course.”

Yichen nodded.

“I appreciate the opportunity to continue. I hope the next stages will be decided by the coaching staff.”

The man looked at him. Then he nodded.

“That’s fair.”

The young player finally spoke.

“Congratulations.”

Yichen turned towards him.

“Thank you.”

There was no hostility in his expression. He didn’t blame the young man for having connections.

He simply didn’t pretend the situation had been fair.

Then Yichen gave a polite nod and continued walking with Xiaoran.

They didn’t speak until they reached the parking area. Xiaoran was holding his hand.

Her fingers were wrapped around his, and she seemed to be thinking hard. Eventually, she looked up.

“You were so cool.”

Yichen glanced at her.

“I’m glad.”

“Very cool.”

He smiled.

“Thank you.”

She walked a little farther before speaking again.

“But I was also a little scared.”

He looked down.

“Why?”

“Because you sounded so serious.”

He laughed.

“Was I frightening?”

“A little.”

“I’m sorry.”

She shook her head.

“No. I liked it.”

He raised an eyebrow.

“You liked being frightened?”

“I liked that you didn’t let them make you feel small.”

He stopped walking. She stopped with him. He studied her.

Then he gently moved a strand of hair away from her face.

“I wasn’t going to argue with them.”

“I know.”

“I just wanted to make my position clear.”

“I know.”

She smiled.

“And you did.”

He looked at her, then kissed her hair.

“Thank you for coming today.”

She blinked.

“Why are you thanking me?”

“Because you’ve been here for every evaluation.”

She smiled.

“Of course.”

“You’ve watched me play.”

“Mm.”

“And you’ve watched me not play.”

She laughed.

“Unfortunately.”

“Still came back.”

She looked at him as if the answer were obvious.

“Yichen.”

“What?”

“I’m your girlfriend.”

He nodded.

“I know.”

“So?”

He laughed.

“Nothing.”

She stepped closer and wrapped her arms around his waist. He held her.
