“Maybe three.”

He laughed again. She immediately looked offended.

“It’s not funny!”

He reached over and pulled her gently towards him.

“All right. I’m sorry.”

She settled sideways on his lap, still looking a little embarrassed. He rested one hand at her waist.

“Listen to me.”

She turned to him.

“You don’t have to repair everything you accidentally damage.”

She lowered her gaze.

“I know.”

“And you certainly don’t have to spend your weekend trying to restore a shirt.”

She was quiet. Yichen brushed a strand of hair behind her ear.

“I know you wanted to fix it because you felt bad. But I would rather have you spend those three hours doing something you enjoy.”

“Like what?”

“Watching your dramas. Eating snacks. Annoying me.”

She laughed despite herself.

“I don’t annoy you.”

“You do.”

“You’re terrible.”

He laughed under his breath.

“Fortunately, I like you.”

She rested her forehead against his shoulder.

“I just wanted to do something nice for you.”

His expression softened. He placed a kiss against her hair.

“You already do.”

A little later, Yichen examined the shirt again. The fabric had recovered some of its shape, though it wasn’t quite the same. The sleeves were still slightly shorter, and the material remained a little different from its original texture. He held it up. Xiaoran stood beside him, watching anxiously.

“Is it okay?”

Yichen looked at the shirt. Then he put it on.

The fit was a little snug around the shoulders, but still wearable. He rolled the sleeves up. Xiaoran studied him.

“Does it feel uncomfortable?”

“No.”

She stepped closer and adjusted the collar.

“It looks different.”

“Does it?”

“A little.”

He held her gaze.

“Do you dislike it?”

She shook her head.

“No. It still looks good.”

His mouth curved.

“Then I’ll keep it.”

“You’re going to wear it?”

“Why not?”

“But it’s smaller.”

“I noticed.”

“Yichen.”

He studied her.

“I like this shirt. I can still wear it. And if it eventually becomes uncomfortable, I’ll stop wearing it.”

She looked at him. Then she smiled.

“Okay.”

He turned slightly.

“How do I look?”

She examined him with exaggerated seriousness.

“Very handsome.”

“Good.”

“Although...”

“Although?”

She reached out and rolled one sleeve a little higher.

“Now you look even better.”

He caught her wrist and kissed the inside of it.

“Your assessment is appreciated.”

She laughed. That evening, Xiaoran was sitting on the sofa, watching a drama while Yichen worked on his laptop. He was still wearing the charcoal shirt. She noticed it several times. Eventually, she paused the episode.

“Yichen?”

“Hm?”

“Can I ask you something?”

He looked up.

“Of course.”

“Was that really one of your favourite shirts?”

He considered the question.

“Yes.”

“Why?”

“Comfortable. Good fabric. Easy to wear.”

She looked down at her hands.

“Did you buy it a long time ago?”

“About two years ago.”

“Oh.”

He watched her.

“Why?”

She shrugged.

“I just wanted to know.”

He closed his laptop.

“Xiaoran.”

She looked up.

“Do you think I liked the shirt more than I like having you around?”

Her eyes widened.

“No!”

“Then why are you still thinking about it?”

She laughed awkwardly.

“I don’t know.”

He moved closer. He opened his arms. She shifted towards him.

He placed an arm around her waist and drew her against his chest.

“Besides,” he said, “I think it has become a rather interesting shirt.”

“Why?”

“Because it has a story now.”

She looked up.

“A story?”

“My girlfriend accidentally shrank it, spent three hours trying to rescue it, and then nearly conducted a scientific experiment in our bedroom.”

Xiaoran covered her face.

“Please don’t tell anyone.”

He laughed.

“I won’t.”

“Especially Fang Ze.”

“Him least of all.”

She relaxed. Then she looked at him again.

“Can I still do the laundry?”

He blinked.

“Why wouldn’t you?”

“Because maybe you don’t trust me anymore.”

Yichen looked at her. Then his expression softened.

“Xiaoran, I’m not going to ban you from doing laundry because one shirt shrank.”

That made her grin.

“Okay.”

“We’ll just pay more attention to the labels.”

She nodded.

“And maybe I shouldn’t put everything in the dryer.”

“That would be a good start.”

She leaned closer and kissed his cheek.

“Thank you for not being angry.”

He turned his face and kissed her lips.

“Thank you for caring.”

She smiled against his mouth. A week later, Xiaoran opened the wardrobe and found something unexpected.

The charcoal shirt was hanging in its usual place. Beside it was a new shirt. Almost identical. Same charcoal-grey colour, similar cut, similar fabric.

She took it off the hanger and examined it.

Then she turned towards Yichen, who was buttoning his watch.

“Did you buy another one?”

He glanced over.

“Yes.”

She looked at the shirt again.

“Why?”

“The old one is a little small.”

“But you said you could still wear it.”

“I can.”

“Then why buy another?”

He finished adjusting his watch.

“Because I liked it.”

She frowned slightly.

“Yichen.”

“What?”

“You really don’t need to replace everything.”

“I know.”

“Then?”

He walked over and took the shirt from her hands, hanging it back in the wardrobe.

“Because I wanted another one.”

She held his gaze. He kissed her.

“The old one stays. The new one is for when I want the original fit.”

She nodded slowly. Then she looked at the two shirts side by side. One new. One slightly imperfect. She reached out and touched the older shirt.

“Are you sure you don’t mind?”

Yichen followed her gaze. Then he put his arm around her waist.

“Not even a little.”

She turned towards him. Her expression softened. He kissed her cheek.

“And for the record, I don’t need you to take care of my belongings perfectly.”

Her mouth tipped up.

“I know.”

“I just need you to stop looking so sad whenever something goes wrong.”

She laughed.

“I’ll try.”

He gave her waist a gentle squeeze.

“Good.”

“Although,” he said, with a smile, “if you’re planning to conduct another experiment, perhaps use one of Fang Ze’s shirts.”

Xiaoran burst out laughing.

“Yichen!”

“What? He has plenty.”

“You’re so mean.”

He smiled and kissed her hair again. The old charcoal shirt stayed in the wardrobe, and Yichen still wore it sometimes.

And every time he did, Xiaoran would look at him with a little smile.

He never told her that he sometimes chose it deliberately. He liked seeing that smile.

chapters.desc: She has forty minutes to get ready for dinner with her friends. He has just come home, and he is in no hurry to let her finish.
chapters.title: An Unexpected Back Hug
chapters.epigraph: “Because you’re here.”
chapters.content:
Xiaoran was halfway through doing her makeup when Yichen came home.

She heard the front door open, followed by the familiar sound of his keys dropping into the bowl by the door.

“I’m home.”

She looked at herself in the mirror.

“Welcome back!”

Yichen walked into the bedroom a moment later, still wearing his training clothes. His hair was slightly damp from his shower at the facility, and he had a sports bag hanging from one shoulder. He stopped at the doorway.

Xiaoran was sitting in front of the dressing table, wearing a pale pink top and a skirt. Her makeup products were arranged across the tabletop, and she was carefully applying mascara with one hand while holding her phone in the other. He watched her for a few seconds.

“Going out?”

“Mm-hm.”

“With your team?”

“No, with Jiayi and Ning. We’re having dinner.”

He put his bag down.

“What time?”

“Seven.”

Yichen glanced at the clock. It was 6:18.

“You’re almost ready?”

“Almost.”

He looked at the number of products spread across the table, then at her face.

“How long have you been getting ready? Not long.”

“How long?”

“Twenty minutes.”

Something in his face eased. She immediately narrowed her eyes at his reflection.

“You’re looking at me like you don’t believe me.”

“I didn’t say anything.”

“You don’t have to.”

He laughed and walked towards the bathroom to wash his hands. Xiaoran returned to her mascara.

She had absolutely no idea that the next twenty minutes would become more difficult.

Yichen returned wearing a clean dark T-shirt and comfortable trousers.

He walked behind her chair, glanced at her reflection, and placed one hand lightly on her shoulder.

“Hello.”

She smiled at him through the mirror.

“Hello.”

He bent down and kissed her temple.

“How was your day?”

“Good. Busy, though.”

“What happened?”

She began telling him about a project at work, explaining how one of her colleagues had changed the direction of a presentation at the last minute. Yichen listened, occasionally asking questions.

His hand moved from her shoulder to her upper arm.

Then, as she continued speaking, he walked around the chair and stood beside her.

She was reaching for her blush when he leaned down and kissed her cheek. Xiaoran smiled.

“You’re interrupting.”

“Sorry.”

He didn’t sound sorry. She dipped her brush into the blush.

“Anyway, as I was saying—”

He kissed her other cheek. She stopped.

“Yichen.”

“Hm?”

“I’m talking.”

“I know.”

“Then listen.”

“I’m listening.”

She looked at him through the mirror. He was smiling. She pointed her brush at him.

“Don’t look at me like that.”

“Like what?”

“That.”

His smile grew.

“All right.”

He walked away. Xiaoran watched him disappear into the living area, then shook her head with a smile. Finally. Peace. She returned to her makeup.

Five minutes later, she was carefully blending eyeshadow when she felt a pair of arms slide around her waist from behind. She startled slightly.

“Ah!”

Yichen rested his chin on her shoulder.

“Sorry.”

She looked at him in the mirror.

“You scared me!”

“You were concentrating.”

“Obviously. I’m doing my makeup.”

He hummed. His hands settled comfortably against her waist, fingers resting just above her hips. Xiaoran tried to continue blending her eyeshadow.

It was difficult. He wasn’t doing anything disruptive. He was there. Warm, close, and entirely too comfortable. She glanced at his reflection.

“Why are you standing like this?”

“Can I not?”

“You can. But I’m doing something.”

“I noticed.”

He kissed the side of her neck, just below her ear. Her brush stopped. Yichen smiled against her skin.

“Continue.”

She turned her head slightly.

“How?”

He laughed.

“Your makeup.”

“You’re the reason I can’t continue.”

He looked at her reflection.

“Would you like me to move?”

Xiaoran considered it. Then, rather than answer, she leaned back against him. Yichen’s smile softened. He tightened his arms slightly around her waist. Neither spoke. Then she lifted her brush again.

“Okay. Now don’t move.”

“All right.”

He lasted about forty seconds. Xiaoran was applying blush to her other cheek when his fingers began tracing small, absentminded circles against her waist. She glanced down.

“Yichen.”

“Hm?”

“Your hand.”

He stopped.

“What’s wrong?”

“You’re tickling me.”

“Sorry.”

She continued. His hand remained still. She was almost finished blending when he leaned forward and kissed her cheek again. She closed her eyes.

“Zhou Yichen.”

He laughed.

“Yes?”

“Are you bored?”

“No.”

“Then why are you bothering me?”

He looked at her reflection.

“Because you’re here.”

She blinked. That was unfair. He knew exactly how to say things like that without making a big deal out of them. She tried to hide her smile.

“That’s not a proper answer.”

“It’s an honest one.”

She met his eyes, then turned her attention back to the mirror.

“Fine. But I need to finish.”

“Go ahead.”

He kissed her temple.

“Take your time.”

Xiaoran moved on to her eyeliner. This was the most delicate part of her makeup, and she needed both concentration and a steady hand. Yichen seemed to understand this.

For the first time since coming home, he became quiet.

His arms remained around her waist, but he didn’t move. Xiaoran was grateful.

She carefully drew the first line, then the second. She leaned back slightly to inspect the result.

“Good.”

Yichen looked at her reflection.

“Looks nice.”

She smiled.

“Thank you.”

She was about to reach for her eyeliner again when he spoke.

“Can I ask you something?”

“Yes.”

“Why are you wearing earrings?”

She turned to him.

“Because they’re pretty.”

He glanced at the small flower-shaped earrings.

“The ones you bought?”

“Yes.”

“They suit you.”

She grinned.

“I know.”

He laughed. She reached for her lipstick. Then felt him press a kiss against her shoulder. She stopped.

“Yichen.”

“Hm?”

“You’re doing it again.”

“What am I doing?”

“Being affectionate.”

He raised his eyebrows.

“Is that a problem?”

She looked at him in the mirror.

“Not normally.”

“Then?”

She held up the lipstick.

“Do you see this?”

He looked at it.

“Yes.”

“I’m trying to apply it.”

“Understood.”

She waited. He didn’t move. She turned her head slightly.

“You’re not going to kiss me while I’m wearing lipstick.”

He didn’t bother hiding the smile.

“Why not?”

“Because you’ll ruin it.”

“Then I’ll wait.”

She looked satisfied.

“Good.”

He lowered his head and kissed her bare cheek instead. Xiaoran stared at him.

“That doesn’t count.”

He laughed. By 6:42, Xiaoran was finally applying lipstick.

Yichen had moved to stand behind her again, his arms loosely around her waist.

She carefully applied the colour, pressed her lips together, then reached for a tissue.

“Almost done.”

Yichen looked at her reflection.

“Pretty.”

“Thank you.”

She leaned towards the mirror to check the corners. He watched her.

Then, gently, he turned her chair a few degrees towards him. Xiaoran looked up.

“What?”

He bent slightly. She immediately raised one finger.

“No.”

He paused. She pointed at her lips.

“Just finished.”

He looked at her, then smiled.

“All right.”

“Good.”

He bent and kissed her hairline. Then her cheek, then the tip of her nose. Xiaoran laughed.

“You’re ridiculous.”

He straightened. She turned back towards the mirror, then looked at her reflection. Her lipstick was intact. She couldn’t help smiling.

“See? You can behave.”

Yichen rested his chin on her shoulder.

“For how long?”

She held his gaze.

“At least until I finish.”

He nodded.

“Understood.”

The final step was perfume. Xiaoran reached for the bottle she had chosen and sprayed a little onto her wrists. Then she turned her head towards Yichen.

“How does it smell?”

He leaned closer to her wrist.

“Nice.”

“Do you like it?”

“Yes.”

She offered the other wrist. He took her hand and brought it closer, smelling the fragrance. Then he kissed the inside of her wrist. Xiaoran looked down at him.

“That’s not how you’re supposed to test perfume.”

Something in his face eased.

“Isn’t it?”

“No.”

He kissed her wrist again. She laughed.

“Yichen!”

He released her hand.

“All right.”

She put the bottle away and looked at herself one last time. Her makeup was finished. Her hair was neat. Her earrings were in place. She was finally ready. She stood up. Yichen’s arms naturally came around her waist again. She tilted her head.

“Finished.”

He glanced at her face, then at her outfit.

“Beautiful.”

“Thank you.”

He brushed his thumb along her waist. He reached for her. She tilted her head.

“Why?”

He leaned down.

“Now I can kiss you.”

She laughed.

“You’ve been kissing me this whole time!”

“Not properly.”

Before she could answer, he kissed her. She wrapped her arms around his shoulders, careful at first because of her lipstick, but he was gentle. His hand rested against her back while the other stayed at her waist.

When he pulled away, he looked at her lips.

“Still intact.”

That made her grin.

“Of course.”

He kissed her once more, this time just at the corner of her mouth.

A few minutes later, Xiaoran was standing near the entrance, checking her handbag. Yichen came to see her off. She glanced at him.

“You’re not coming with me, right?”

He looked up.

“No. I have something to review.”

“Okay.”

He walked towards her.

“Have fun.”

“I will.”

He adjusted the strap of her bag where it had twisted against her shoulder.

“Text me when you arrive.”

“I will.”

“And when you’re leaving.”

She laughed.

“Yes, Zhou Yichen.”

He smiled and kissed her hair. She was about to open the door when he caught her hand.

“Wait.”

She turned.

“What?”

He met her eyes. Then gently pulled her back towards him, wrapping his arms around her waist. Xiaoran looked up.

“Another one?”

“One more.”

She laughed.

“You’re very clingy today.”

He lowered his head. He kissed her cheek. Then her forehead. Then, after a brief pause, he smiled.

“Have I ruined your makeup?”

She examined his face.

“No.”

“Good.”

She reached up and adjusted the collar of his shirt.

“Although you’ve made me late.”

He glanced at the clock.

“By three minutes.”

“Three important minutes.”

He laughed.

“Sorry.”

She kissed his cheek.

“Forgiven.”

Then she finally left. A little after eight, Yichen received a photograph.

It was a selfie of Xiaoran at the restaurant, sitting between Jiayi and Ning. Her makeup still looked perfect.

Xiaoran: Look! My makeup survived.

He smiled.

Yichen: Impressive.

Xiaoran: You didn’t ruin it.

Yichen: You’re welcome.

Xiaoran: Don’t be so proud. I did all the work.

Yichen: I provided moral support.

She sent him a laughing sticker. A few seconds later, another message arrived.

Xiaoran: Actually, I miss you.

Yichen looked at the message, then replied.

Yichen: Enjoy dinner. I’ll be here when you get back.

She sent a heart. He put his phone down and returned to his tablet.

When Xiaoran returned home that night, it was nearly eleven.

She opened the door, expecting Yichen to have gone to bed.

Instead, she found him sitting on the sofa with his laptop open. He looked up.

“Back?”

That made her grin.

“Mm-hm.”

“Had fun?”

“Very much.”

He closed his laptop and stood. She walked towards him, immediately slipping her arms around his waist. Yichen looked down.

“What’s this?”

“A hug.”

“I can see that.”

She rested her cheek against his chest, then looked up.

“Did you miss me?”

He brushed her hair away from her face.

“The apartment was too quiet.”

She laughed.

“Poor you.”

“Very.”

He kissed her, briefly. She pulled away slightly and pointed at her face.

“Look.”

He examined her.

“What?”

“My makeup is still perfect.”

That got a smile out of him.

“Congratulations.”

She narrowed her eyes.

“You’re not impressed?”

“I am.”

She smiled proudly.

“See? I can go out, have fun, and come home with everything intact.”

Yichen nodded.

“Very capable.”

She leaned closer.

“Although...”

“Hm?”

“I think I might need to redo my lipstick.”

He turned to her.

“Why?”

She smiled mischievously.

“Because someone kept trying to kiss me earlier.”

Yichen’s mouth curved into that slow, knowing smile.

“Is that so?”

She nodded. He stepped closer, his hands finding her waist as naturally as ever.

“Then perhaps I should make it worth reapplying.”

Xiaoran’s cheeks warmed.

“Yichen.”

He laughed and kissed her. This time, she didn’t have to worry about finishing her makeup.

And when they finally separated, she looked up at him with a smile.

“You’re terrible.”

He brushed his thumb over her cheek.

“Yet you keep coming back.”

She laughed and hugged him again.

“Unfortunately.”

Yichen kissed her hair. He knew perfectly well she didn’t mean it.

chapters.desc: A balcony door that locks itself, eleven floors up, and the friend who has had their spare key since moving day.
chapters.title: The Spare Key Incident
chapters.epigraph: “I didn’t save you. Fang Ze did.”
chapters.content:
The first mistake was leaving the balcony door open. The second was shutting it. The third, and by some distance the worst, was assuming Zhou Yichen remembered where the spare key was.

“Yichen?”

“Mm.”

Lin Xiaoran was standing in the middle of the balcony with two mugs of tea. “Did you lock the door?”

He looked up from his phone. Then past her, at the glass door. The handle was down. She followed his eyes, put the mugs on the little table, and tried it. Once. Twice. She turned round slowly.

“Yichen.”

He got up. “Wait.”

She tried the handle a third time, as if it might respond to a more optimistic attitude. It didn’t. The latch had dropped when the door swung shut in the wind, and the only way to lift it was from inside.

For a few seconds neither of them said anything.

It was a mild evening in March. The city lights were coming on below. They had two chairs, a small table, two cups of tea, and the potted lemon tree she had been trying to keep alive since Moving Day. They were also eleven floors up, and the only way back into their flat was through a locked glass door.

“Have you got your phone?” he said.

She held it up.

“Good.” He held up his.

“Why are you so calm?”

“Because we’re not in danger.”

“We’re locked out.”

“On our balcony.”

“That’s still locked out.”

“All right,” he said, and tried the handle himself, and looked at the frame, and the latch through the glass, with the expression of a man who believed most problems would give in if he concentrated hard enough.

“Can you break it?” she said.

“No.”

“Why not?”

“Because it’s our door.”

“That’s a very good point.”

“Thank you. I’ll ring Fang Ze,” he said, and unlocked his phone.

“Why Fang Ze?”

“He’s got our spare key.”

She stared at him. Then at the door. Then at him.

“Why does Fang Ze have our spare key?”

“Because he lives ten minutes away.”

It wasn’t an answer, and they both knew it.

“I gave it to him on Moving Day. In case.”

“You gave Fang Ze a key to our home? Without telling me?”

“I told you.”

“When?”

“On Moving Day. While I was giving it to him. You were standing right there.”

She opened her mouth. She shut it. She thought back. Then she pointed at him.

“I was carrying a box.”

“You were.”

“A heavy box. I was very busy.”

“I noticed.”

“You should have reminded me.”

“I’ll remind you next time,” he said, and she looked at him with deep disapproval, and he pressed call.

✦ ✦ ✦

Fang Ze picked up on the third ring. “Captain?”

He still called him that, from their last year on the university team, although Yichen hadn’t been captain of anything for nearly two years.

“Are you home?”

“Yes. What’s up?”

“Have you still got our spare key?”

A pause. “Why?”

Yichen looked at Xiaoran. “We’re locked out.”

“Where?”

“On the balcony.”

There was a silence on the line. Then a sound, which wasn’t quite a laugh yet.

“You’re joking.”

“I’m not.”

“How?”

Xiaoran leaned over his arm towards the phone. “Don’t ask how. Just come and rescue us.”

Fang Ze started laughing properly. Tell him to hurry, she mouthed.

“Can you come over?”

“Of course. Give me fifteen minutes.”

“Thank you.”

“Wait, wait. You’re both actually outside? Right now? On your own balcony?”

“Yes, Fang Ze.”

Fang Ze laughed so much he had to put the phone down, and they heard him from a distance saying sorry, sorry, he was coming, and then the line went dead.

Xiaoran looked at the city. At the door. At the two cups of tea.

“Well,” she said.

Yichen pulled out one of the chairs for her. “Sit down.”

“You’re treating this like a picnic.”

“We’ve got tea.”

“We’re locked out of our home.”

“We’ve also got tea,” he said, and she looked at him, and then sat.

✦ ✦ ✦

Five minutes later she was regretting several things. Not bringing a cardigan. Agreeing to come out here at all. And having a boyfriend who seemed perfectly content to treat being trapped on a balcony as a minor change to the evening’s schedule. She rubbed her arms. He noticed at once.

“Cold?”

“A bit.”

He took his jacket off and put it round her shoulders, and then, because the chairs were too far apart, picked his chair up and put it right next to hers, and sat down, and pulled her against his side. They watched the traffic for a while.

“Do you think Fang Ze will tell the team?” she said.

“Probably.”

“Yichen.”

“He’ll tell Kou Ran.”

“And Kou Ran will tell everybody.”

“Probably.”

She groaned and put her face in his shoulder. “We’re never going to hear the end of this.”

“Maybe not.”

“You’re not worried?”

“No.”

“Why not?”

“Because it’s funny,” he said, and she lifted her head and stared at him.

“You’re enjoying this.”

He didn’t deny it. He tucked the jacket more firmly round her shoulders. “At least we’re locked out together.”

“That’s a very romantic way to describe being trapped.”

“Would you rather I said I regret being here?”

She thought about it. “No.”

“Then we’re fine,” he said, and she put her head back on his shoulder and drank her cooling tea.

At twelve minutes her phone buzzed.

Fang Ze: nearly there. stopping at the shop downstairs. want anything?

Xiaoran: hot milk tea please

Xiaoran: half sugar no pearls

Xiaoran: thank you savior

“You’re ordering drinks?” said Yichen.

“We’re waiting.”

“We’ve got tea.”

“It’s cold now,” she said, and he looked at his mug, and couldn’t argue.

Fang Ze: you’re welcome. please don’t lock yourselves out again

Fang Ze: actually can I take a photo when I get there

She sat bolt upright. “No.”

He took the phone out of her hand and typed.

Xiaoran: Just bring the key.

Fang Ze replied with a laughing face.

“He’s going to be unbearable,” she said.

“He’s already unbearable,” said Yichen, and handed the phone back.

✦ ✦ ✦

At twenty minutes they heard the front door open inside the flat, and Fang Ze’s voice down the hall.

“Captain?”

“Balcony,” Yichen called through the glass.

Fang Ze came into the living room with a plastic bag in one hand and stopped dead. He looked at Yichen standing at the glass door. He looked at Xiaoran in the chair behind him, wrapped in Yichen’s jacket. He looked at the latch. And then he started laughing, helplessly, bent over with his hand on the back of the sofa.

Xiaoran pointed at him through the glass. “Don’t.”

“I’m sorry.”

“You’re not!”

“You’re right,” he said, and lifted the latch, and slid the door open. It was the most beautiful sound she had heard all evening. She went straight past him into the warm flat.

“Thank you.”

Fang Ze bowed. “You’re welcome.”

He turned to Yichen.

“Captain. I didn’t know you were capable of something like this,” said Fang Ze.

“It was an accident.”

“With Xiaoran?”

“Why are you saying it like that?” said Xiaoran.

Fang Ze raised both hands. “Nothing. Nothing at all. Your milk tea.” He held out the bag.

“You actually got it!”

“I was downstairs anyway. I think I deserve more than thank you, though.” He watched her take it.

“What do you want?” said Yichen.

“Dinner. And one photo.”

“No.”

“Just one.”

Xiaoran stepped behind Yichen with the milk tea. “No photos.”

“You’re both very protective of your dignity,” said Fang Ze. He went to the door. Then he stopped and turned back, with the key in his hand. “Do you want this back, or shall I keep it?”

There was a long silence. Xiaoran and Yichen looked at each other.

“Maybe you should keep it,” said Xiaoran carefully.

“Wise,” said Fang Ze, and put it back on his own keyring, and went.

✦ ✦ ✦

That should have been the end of it. It wasn’t, because Fang Ze had Kou Ran’s number, and Kou Ran was in the Herons team chat.

By breakfast the next morning Yichen’s phone was buzzing on the table every few seconds.

Kou Ran: heard the captain had a difficult evening

Qin Lei: what happened

Kou Ran: Fang Ze says he got locked out

Bao Dong: of what

Kou Ran: his balcony

Qin Lei: WHAT

Bao Dong: HOW

Kou Ran: with Xiaoran

Qin Lei: together??

Kou Ran: on their own balcony. for twenty minutes. eleven floors up

Bao Dong: Zhou please explain

Xiaoran looked up from her congee. “What’s happening?”

“Nothing.”

“Yichen.”

He turned the phone off. “Kou Ran.”

“Of course it’s Kou Ran.”

It buzzed again. He looked at it, and this time he actually smiled, and turned it round so she could see.

Kou Ran: Zhou, next time you want fresh air, try a window

She put her face in her hands. “I’m going to kill Fang Ze.”

“Kou Ran,” he said.

“Both of them.”

✦ ✦ ✦

That afternoon she found him at the balcony door, testing the latch. He opened it. Closed it. Opened it. Looked at the latch from the outside.

“What are you doing?”

“Checking it.”

“It works perfectly. We were the problem.”

“That’s true,” he said, and propped the door open with the lemon tree.

She stepped out onto the balcony and looked round. “We should hide a key out here. In case.”

“Where?”

Her eyes went to the table, the lemon tree, the railing.

“No,” he said.

“What?”

“Don’t hide a key in the plant pot.”

“I wasn’t going to.”

“Not necessarily,” she said.

He laughed, and put his hand in his pocket, and held out a small key.

“What’s that?”

“A spare.”

“Another one?”

“Since we moved in.”

“Where was it last night?”

“In the kitchen drawer.”

“Inside the flat.”

“Inside the flat,” he agreed.

“Why didn’t you tell me there was another one?”

“I thought you knew.”

She took the key out of his hand and looked at it, and at him. “Zhou Yichen. You’re lucky I love you.”

“Very lucky,” he said.

He took the key back, crouched down, and taped it to the underside of the balcony table with two strips of the tape her father had sent up in November, where nobody would ever see it unless they were lying on the floor. She watched him do it.

“That’s a good place.”

“I know.”

She caught his sleeve before he could go back in and pulled him round and kissed him on the balcony, in the sun, eleven floors up, with the door wide open behind them.

“What was that for?”

“For saving me.”

“I didn’t save you. Fang Ze did.”

“Then I’ll thank him next time.”

“Let’s hope there isn’t one,” he said, and moved the lemon tree back, and shut the door carefully from the inside.

chapters.desc: An ordinary Wednesday, a dark suit, and a dinner he planned because they keep eating between calls.
chapters.title: A Night Worth Dressing Up For
chapters.epigraph: “I wanted an evening where neither of us had to think about anything else.”
chapters.content:
Xiaoran knew something was happening when Yichen came home and didn’t immediately change into his usual comfortable clothes.

He had just returned from an afternoon meeting and training session. Usually, the first thing he did after entering their apartment was loosen his watch, put his phone down, and head for the shower. Today, however, he walked straight into the bedroom.

Xiaoran was sitting on the bed with her laptop, editing a presentation. She looked up when he entered.

“You’re home.”

“Mm.”

He pressed a kiss to her temple. Then he opened the wardrobe. Xiaoran watched him take out a dark suit. She blinked, then blinked again.

“Yichen?”

“Hm?”

“What are you doing?”

He hung the suit carefully on the wardrobe door.

“Getting ready.”

“For what?”

“Dinner.”

She met his eyes.

“With whom?”

He turned around.

“With you.”

There was a brief silence. Xiaoran slowly closed her laptop.

“Are we going somewhere?”

“Yes.”

“Where?”

“Somewhere nice.”

She eyed him.

“That’s not an answer.”

Yichen smiled.

“You’re right.”

He walked towards her, bent down, and placed a hand beside her on the mattress.

“It’s a surprise.”

Her eyes immediately brightened.

“A surprise?”

“Yes.”

“What kind of surprise?”

“Dinner.”

“Yichen!”

He laughed and kissed her cheek.

“Six thirty. Take your time getting ready.”

She caught his wrist before he could straighten up.

“Wait. What should I wear?”

“Something you feel beautiful in.”

She stared at him. He didn’t bother hiding the smile.

“That’s all the guidance you’re getting.”

And then he left the bedroom. Xiaoran looked at the closed door, then at the suit, then back at the door. She slowly reached for her phone. There was only one reasonable thing to do. She needed to investigate.

By five o’clock, the bedroom had become a small fashion crisis. Three dresses were lying across the bed. One was too casual. One was too elaborate.

One was beautiful, but she couldn’t decide whether it was appropriate for a surprise dinner.

Xiaoran stood in front of the mirror wearing a simple satin dress, looking at herself from different angles. She liked it. But was it too much?

She picked up her phone and took a picture, then deleted it. She took another. Deleted that one too. Eventually, she walked out of the bedroom.

Yichen was standing in the living room, fastening his watch. He had already changed.

A dark tailored suit, a crisp white shirt, and a discreet watch. His hair was neatly styled, and he had chosen a fragrance that was familiar to her: woody, elegant, and subtle. He looked up. His eyes settled on her. He didn’t say anything.

Xiaoran became aware of the dress she was wearing.

“What?”

Yichen’s gaze moved over her once, unhurriedly.

“Nothing.”

“Why are you looking at me?”

“Because you’re beautiful.”

She looked away, her face warm. He approached her.

The closer he came, the more she noticed how well he was dressed. It wasn’t unusual for Yichen to look handsome, but tonight he seemed put together.

He stopped in front of her and adjusted one of the straps on her shoulder.

“This one?”

She nodded. He looked at her again, and took his time about it. Then he smiled.

“You’re going to make it difficult for me to concentrate on dinner.”

Her cheeks warmed.

“You’re exaggerating.”

“Possibly.”

He offered his hand.

“Shall we?”

Xiaoran had expected him to order a car. Instead, Yichen led her down to the private parking area.

She followed him to his car, the one she had once driven round the bottom level of this car park at twenty kilometres an hour. He unlocked it. Xiaoran looked at the car, then at him.

“This one?”

“Yes.”

“Why?”

“Because I feel like driving tonight.”

Her mouth tipped up.

“You’re taking me on a date in this car?”

“I’m taking you on a date. The car is just transportation.”

She laughed.

“That’s a very Zhou Yichen answer.”

He opened the passenger door for her. Before getting in, she looked at him.

“Wait.”

He raised an eyebrow.

“What?”

She stepped closer and straightened his lapel.

“You look very handsome.”

His expression softened.

“Thank you.”

She patted his chest once, satisfied.

“Okay. Now you can drive.”

Yichen laughed and closed the door after she settled in.

Inside, the car was quiet and comfortable. The leather seats were cool against her skin, and the subtle scent of his car mixed with the fragrance he wore. He started the engine.

Xiaoran buckled her seat belt and looked at him.

“Can I ask where we’re going?”

“You can ask.”

“Will you tell me?”

“No.”

She gasped. He smiled as he pulled out of the parking space.

The restaurant was in one of the city’s most exclusive districts.

It occupied the upper floor of a beautiful building, with a private entrance, discreet staff, and a view of the city skyline.

When the car stopped at the entrance, Xiaoran looked out of the window. Then she looked at Yichen.

“Wait.”

He unbuckled his seat belt.

“What?”

“Is this...?”

He got out before she could finish. A moment later, her door opened. Yichen offered his hand. She took it, stepping out carefully.

The restaurant’s entrance was elegant without being overly extravagant. Warm lighting spilled through the glass doors, and the staff greeted Yichen with quiet familiarity. Xiaoran glanced at him.

“You’ve been here before?”

“Once.”

“With whom?”

He met her eyes.

“The club’s sponsors’ dinner.”

She nodded.

“Ah.”

He rested his hand lightly against her lower back as they entered.

The host greeted him by name and led them through the restaurant.

Their table was positioned beside a large window, overlooking the illuminated city. It was private enough for conversation, but not so secluded that it felt formal or uncomfortable. Xiaoran looked around.

The table was beautifully arranged, with delicate flowers, polished cutlery, and soft candlelight. She sat down slowly.

“Yichen.”

“Hm?”

“This is really nice.”

“I’m glad.”

She looked at the menu, then looked at the prices. Her eyes widened slightly. She quickly lowered it. Yichen noticed. He didn’t comment immediately.

Instead, he took his seat opposite her and unfolded his napkin.

“Do you like the view?”

She nodded.

“Very much.”

“Good.”

He picked up the menu.

“I thought you’d enjoy somewhere quieter tonight.”

Xiaoran looked at him.

“Why?”

He met her eyes.

“Because we’ve both been busy.”

She softened.

“That’s true.”

“Your deadlines have been piling up, and my schedule hasn’t been particularly flexible lately. We keep having dinner at home, eating between calls, or rushing because one of us has somewhere to be. I wanted an evening where neither of us had to think about anything else.”

Xiaoran looked at him. Then she smiled.

“You planned all this just because you wanted to have dinner with me?”

“Is that insufficient?”

“No.”

She shook her head.

“It’s very sufficient.”

His lips curved.

“Then let’s enjoy it.”

The dinner was everything Xiaoran had expected from an elite restaurant and more.

The staff explained each course with quiet precision. The presentation was beautiful, but the food wasn’t merely decorative. Every dish had its own flavour and texture, and Yichen had chosen a tasting menu with a few additional dishes he thought she might enjoy. Xiaoran was interested in the dessert.

She examined it from every angle before tasting it. Yichen watched her.

“What?”

She took another photograph.

“Nothing. It’s pretty.”

“Do you want me to take a picture of you?”

She looked up. She smiled and handed him her phone.

He took several pictures, adjusting the angle when she asked him to.

“Wait, the lighting is too dark.”

He moved the phone slightly.

“Like this?”

“Yes.”

“Look here.”

She smiled. He took the picture, then another. And another.

When he handed the phone back, she examined the photos.

“Oh.”

“Good?”

“Very good.”

She looked up at him.

“You’re surprisingly good at this.”

“I’ve had practice.”

“With whom?”

He gave her a look. She laughed.

“Right. Me.”

He reached across the table and gently touched her fingers.

“Who else?”

She smiled and turned her attention back to the dessert. Yichen watched her take the first bite. Her expression changed immediately. He raised an eyebrow.

“Good?”

She nodded enthusiastically.

“Very.”

He moved his own dessert slightly towards her.

“Try mine.”

She tasted it, then looked at him.

“Yours is better.”

“Then we’ll exchange.”

She looked at his plate.

“Really?”

“Yes.”

She pushed her dessert towards him. He accepted it without complaint. Xiaoran smiled.

“You’re very generous tonight.”

“Only tonight?”

She pretended to consider.

“Most nights.”

“That’s better.”

After the main course, the conversation became slower. There was no need to hurry.

They talked about work, her latest project at Morrow Studio, and an upcoming away game that would take Yichen out of Shanghai for several days.

Xiaoran told him about a client who wanted the logo bigger in every frame, including the one where it was already on the side of a building. Yichen listened, occasionally asking questions. Then she asked about his training.

He told her about a tactical adjustment the coach had been discussing and how the team had been working on defensive transitions.

She listened carefully, even though some of the terminology still confused her. At one point, she frowned.

“Wait. So if the opponent does that, you have to move there?”

“Not exactly.”

“Then where?”

He explained it again, using the edge of his napkin to sketch a rough court layout. Xiaoran leaned forward.

“Oh.”

“Understand?”

“Mostly.”

“Mostly?”

“I understand the drawing. I don’t understand why everyone has to run so much.”

He laughed.

“That’s basketball.”

She shook her head.

“Your job is very tiring.”

“It can be.”

She turned to him.

“Are you happy?”

The question came naturally, without any particular reason. Yichen looked at her, then nodded.

“Yes.”

“Good.”

He reached for his glass.

“And you?”

“Happy?”

“With work.”

She thought.

“Yes. Tired, sometimes. A little overwhelmed, sometimes. But I like what I’m doing.”

“Good.”

She tilted her head.

“You’re asking like a very serious interviewer.”

“I want to know.”

Her expression softened.

“I know.”

They looked at each other. Then Xiaoran reached across the table and placed her hand over his.

“Thank you for tonight.”

Yichen turned his hand beneath hers, holding it.

“You’re welcome.”

After dinner, Yichen didn’t immediately take her home. Instead, he suggested they walk along the terrace outside the restaurant.

The city was bright beneath them, with traffic moving like streams of light through the streets. Xiaoran stood beside the railing, looking out.

Yichen came to stand behind her, his hands resting lightly at her waist. She leaned back against him.

“It’s beautiful.”

“Mm.”

She turned her head slightly.

“Do you come here often?”

“Not really.”

“Why?”

“Never had much reason to.”

She held his gaze. He smiled.

“Until tonight.”

She laughed.

“You’re being romantic.”

He lowered his head and kissed her temple. She turned around in his arms.

His suit jacket was still perfectly arranged, although she could see that his tie had loosened slightly during dinner. She reached up and adjusted it.

“You’re very handsome tonight.”

“You’ve mentioned that.”

“I know. I want to mention it again.”

His mouth curved.

“Then I’ll accept the compliment again.”

She laughed. Then she looked at him more closely.

“Actually, you know what?”

“What?”

“I like seeing you dressed like this.”

He raised an eyebrow.

“Why?”

“Because you usually come home in training clothes or comfortable clothes. Sometimes you look like you’ve just fought an entire basketball team.”

“I usually have.”

She laughed.

“But tonight, you look like... A very successful businessman.” She paused, searching for the right words.

That got a smile out of him.

“Is that a compliment?”

“Yes.”

“Then thank you.”

She tilted her head.

“But I like you in your basketball clothes, too.”

“I know.”

“And your ordinary clothes.”

“I know.”

“And when you’re wearing those ridiculous old T-shirts at home.”

He looked down at her.

“Ridiculous?”

“Some of them are.”

He laughed. She smiled, then wrapped her arms around his waist.

“Basically, I like you in everything.”

Yichen’s expression softened. He lowered his head and kissed her cheek.

“That’s fortunate.”

“Why?”

“Because I don’t plan on changing.”

The drive home was quieter. Xiaoran sat comfortably in the passenger seat, one hand resting on the centre console. Yichen drove with one hand on the steering wheel, the other occasionally reaching over to hold hers. The city lights passed across his face. She looked at him for a while.

Then said, “Can I tell you something?”

“Of course.”

“I was a little nervous when you told me to dress up.”

He glanced at her.

“Why?”

“I thought maybe we were going somewhere really formal. I wasn’t sure what to wear.”

“You looked beautiful.”

“I know. You told me.”

She said, “But I was also excited.”

“Good.”

“Because you planned everything.”

He squeezed her hand.

“I wanted to.”

She looked out of the window.

“Sometimes I feel like we spend so much time managing our schedules that we forget to have proper dates.”

Then he said, “We can make time.”

She turned towards him.

“Even with your training?”

“Even with training.”

“And my deadlines?”

“We’ll work around them.”

He said, “We don’t have to go somewhere expensive every time. But I don’t want us to get so comfortable that we stop making an effort.”

Xiaoran looked at him. There was something about the way he said it that made her heart feel unusually full. She squeezed his hand.

“I don’t think you could ever make me feel like you stopped making an effort.”

He turned to her.

“Good.”

“Although I wouldn’t mind another dinner like this.”

Yichen laughed.

“I thought you might say that.”

When they arrived home, Yichen parked the car and came around to open her door.

Xiaoran stepped out, then waited while he locked the car.

She reached for his hand as they walked towards the elevator.

Just before the doors closed, she turned towards him.

“Yichen?”

“Hm?”

“Next time, I’ll plan the date.”

He held her gaze.

“All right.”

“Properly.”

“I look forward to it.”

“And I’ll take you somewhere nice.”

He laughed under his breath.

“Sounds good.”

She nodded, satisfied.

Then added, “But you have to wear something handsome.”

He glanced down at his suit.

“Like this?”

“Maybe.”

“Maybe?”

She grinned.

“I’ll decide later.”

Yichen shook his head, amused. When they reached their apartment, he helped her take off her coat and hung it up.

She removed her earrings and placed them on the dresser, then turned around to find him watching her.

“What?”

He approached her.

“Nothing.”

She couldn’t help smiling.

“You’re looking at me again.”

“I like looking at you.”

She went quiet. Yichen brushed his thumb over her cheek.

“Did you have a good evening?”

“Very good.”

“Good.”

She pulled him down by the collar and kissed him. Once, then again, a little longer. When she pulled away, he was smiling.

“What’s that for?”

“For planning a date with me.”

“I thought that was what the date was for.”

She laughed. He drew her closer and kissed her temple.

Then, with a faint smile, he said, “You don’t have to wait for a special occasion to ask me out, Xiaoran.”

“I know.”

“Or to dress up.”

“I know.”

“Or to spend an evening together.”

She looked up at him.

“I know.”

He kissed her cheek.

“But I like giving you reasons to look forward to something.”

Her arms tightened around his waist. And for a while, neither of them moved.

What she would remember wasn’t the view. It was the way he had opened the passenger door. The way he had watched her enjoy dessert.

The way he had listened to her talk about work.

And the way he had made an ordinary Wednesday feel like an occasion worth dressing up for. She smiled against his chest.

“Yichen?”

“Hm?”

“Next Wednesday?”

He laughed.

“Already planning the next one?”

“Just checking your availability.”

He pressed his mouth to her hair.

“For you? I’ll make time.”

chapters.desc: A cleaning schedule on the kitchen whiteboard, a free Sunday, and two people who keep getting distracted.
chapters.title: A Very Unproductive Sunday
chapters.epigraph: “We have the rest of the week to clean. I’d rather spend today with you.”
chapters.content:
The plan was simple. Clean the apartment in the morning.

Wash the bedsheets. Vacuum the floors. Wipe the kitchen counters. Organise the wardrobe. Refill the household supplies. Maybe rearrange the living room a little.

By six in the evening, the apartment would be spotless, and they would have the rest of Sunday to themselves.

At least, that was what Xiaoran had written on the small whiteboard in the kitchen.

SUNDAY PLAN
9:00 — Breakfast
9:30 — Laundry
10:00 — Bedroom
11:00 — Living room
12:00 — Lunch
13:00 — Kitchen
14:00 — Bathroom
15:00 — Organise wardrobe
16:00 — Rest

Yichen had looked at the list the previous night.

“You’re very ambitious.”

Xiaoran had been pleased with herself.

“We have a whole day.”

“Mm.”

“And we’re both free.”

“Yes.”

“So we should use it properly.”

He had looked at her before smiling.

“All right, Manager Lin.”

She had pointed her marker at him.

“Don’t think you can escape your responsibilities.”

He had laughed. Now, well before ten on Sunday morning, Yichen was discovering that the plan had already encountered its first obstacle. The obstacle was his girlfriend.

More specifically, his girlfriend was lying on the kitchen counter. Not sitting on a chair. Not standing beside the counter.

Actually lying on it, with her upper body stretched across the cool marble surface while she watched him prepare breakfast. Yichen glanced over from the stove.

“Xiaoran.”

“Hm?”

“What are you doing?”

“Supervising.”

He met her eyes.

“From there?”

“It’s a good view.”

He turned back to the eggs.

“Of what?”

“You.”

His mouth curved.

“Very productive.”

“I know.”

She watched him for a few seconds, then reached out and tugged gently at the hem of his shirt.

“Yichen.”

“Hm?”

“Can you make mine a little softer?”

“Your eggs?”

“Yes.”

He turned off the stove, divided the eggs between two plates, and placed hers in front of her.

“Anything else?”

She looked at the plate, then at him.

“A kiss.”

He kissed her hair. She frowned.

“That’s not what I meant.”

“Then you should be more specific.”

She lifted her face. He understood immediately and kissed her properly, one hand resting against the counter beside her. When he straightened, Xiaoran was smiling.

“Thank you.”

“You’re welcome.”

He returned to breakfast. Xiaoran watched him for another moment.

Then she looked at the whiteboard visible from the kitchen. 9:30 — Laundry. It was already 9:50. She decided not to mention it. By 10:25, they had managed to finish breakfast.

They had also managed to spend fifteen minutes discussing whether the little ceramic bowl Xiaoran had bought last week was suitable for holding fruit. Yichen thought it was. Xiaoran thought it might be too small.

They eventually agreed to put it on the dining table and see how it looked.

Then she wanted to take a photograph. Then Yichen appeared in the background of the photograph. Then she asked him to move.

Then she decided she liked the photograph better with him in it.

By the time they finished, the breakfast dishes were still on the table. Yichen looked at the clock.

“Ten thirty.”

Xiaoran followed his gaze.

“Oh.”

“Should we start?”

“Yes.”

He picked up the plates. She picked up the cups. They carried everything to the kitchen. Yichen washed while Xiaoran dried. For a while, they worked efficiently.

Then Xiaoran noticed that the sleeve of his shirt had slipped down.

“Your sleeve.”

He glanced at it.

“What about it?”

“It’s wet.”

He rolled it up.

“Better?”

She nodded. Then, because his forearm was right there, she reached out and touched it. Yichen looked at her. Something in his face eased.

“You’re distracting me.”

“I’m not doing anything.”

“You’re holding my arm.”

She looked down. She was. She let go.

“Sorry.”

He rinsed the plate. A moment later, she reached for his hand again. He laughed.

“Xiaoran.”

“What?”

“Do you want to finish the dishes or not?”

“Yes.”

“Then let me finish this one.”

She nodded obediently. He placed the clean plate on the rack. She immediately leaned over and kissed his cheek.

“Good job.”

He turned his head slightly.

“Is that my reward?”

That made her grin.

“Would you like another?”

“Yes.”

She kissed his other cheek. Yichen looked at her. Then he put the dishcloth down. He crooked a finger at her.

She barely had time to laugh before he drew her closer and kissed her.

It wasn’t a long kiss, but when they parted, Xiaoran was smiling so brightly that Yichen knew they had just lost another few minutes. He glanced towards the sink. There were still two cups. He turned to her.

“You’re a terrible assistant.”

She gasped.

“I’m an excellent assistant!”

“Your performance says otherwise.”

She reached for the dishcloth.

“Fine. I’ll do it myself.”

He laughed and handed it to her. A little after eleven, they finally entered the bedroom.

Xiaoran stood at the foot of the bed, holding a fresh set of bedsheets.

“First, we need to change these.”

Yichen pulled the blanket away.

“All right.”

They stripped the bed together. Yichen handled the fitted sheet while Xiaoran gathered the pillowcases.

It was going surprisingly well until she attempted to tuck one corner of the sheet under the mattress. The elastic slipped. She tried again. It slipped again. She frowned at it.

“Why is this so difficult?”

Yichen looked over.

“Which corner?”

“This one.”

He walked around the bed.

“Here.”

He crouched and pulled the fabric into place.

“Hold this.”

She held the edge. He stretched the opposite side, and together they secured it.

“There.”

Xiaoran looked at the neatly fitted sheet.

“Good.”

Yichen straightened.

“Next?”

She looked at the pillows, then at the bed, then at him.

“Wait.”

“What?”

She climbed onto the mattress and sat in the middle. Yichen watched her.

“Xiaoran.”

“Just a second.”

She patted the sheet.

“It’s clean.”

“Yes.”

“And soft.”

“Yes.”

She leaned backward, testing it. Then she lay down. Yichen stared. She looked up at him. She opened her arms. He glanced at the pillowcases.

“We haven’t finished.”

“Just for a minute.”

He knew that expression. It was the same one she used when she wanted something but intended to pretend it was a small request.

He climbed onto the bed and lay beside her. Xiaoran immediately rolled towards him. She tucked her head under his chin. Yichen rested one arm around her waist. For a little while, they lay there. Then Xiaoran shifted.

“Yichen?”

“Hm?”

“Do you think we should change the pillows too?”

He looked at the pillows beside them.

“They’re fine.”

“What about the duvet?”

“Also fine.”

“Maybe we should wash the mattress protector.”

“We can.”

She nodded. Then she closed her eyes. Yichen looked down at her.

“Are you sleeping?”

“No.”

“Your eyes are closed.”

“I’m resting them.”

He laughed under his breath.

“Of course.”

A few minutes passed. Then he felt her hand move against his chest.

“Yichen.”

“Yes?”

“Can I ask something?”

“Go ahead.”

“Do you think we’re very lazy?”

He looked at the ceiling.

“Not yet.”

She laughed into his shirt. At noon, they were still in the bedroom. The bedsheets had been changed. The pillows had been replaced. But neither of them had left the bed.

Yichen was lying on his back, one arm behind his head. Xiaoran was practically draped over him, scrolling through her phone. She laughed. He glanced down.

“What?”

“Look.”

She turned her phone towards him. It was a short video of a couple attempting to clean their apartment, only to end up dancing with a mop. Yichen watched until the end.

“Accurate.”

She gasped.

“Are you saying we’re like that?”

“We’ve been in this room for nearly an hour.”

“We changed the sheets!”

“An impressive achievement.”

She smacked his chest lightly.

“You’re supposed to support me.”

“I am.”

He looked at the phone again.

“Perhaps we should dance with the mop.”

She burst out laughing. Then she put her phone down and rested her chin on his chest.

“Let’s get up.”

“All right.”

Neither moved. She waited. Yichen waited. A few seconds later, she smiled.

“You’re not getting up.”

“Neither are you.”

“Because you’re holding me.”

He looked at his arm around her waist.

“Would you like me to let go?”

She considered it, then shook her head.

“No.”

He smiled.

“Then we’re staying.”

Their lunch was supposed to be simple. There were leftovers in the refrigerator, and Yichen suggested reheating them. Xiaoran agreed.

They made it to the kitchen a little before one.

She opened the refrigerator while Yichen took out the containers.

“There’s still some chicken.”

“Mm.”

“And vegetables.”

“Yes.”

“And rice.”

“Good.”

She looked at the ingredients, then at him.

“Actually, I want something else.”

Yichen paused.

“What would you like?”

“Something crispy.”

He looked at the refrigerator.

“Like what?”

She thought.

“Potatoes.”

“We don’t have potatoes.”

“Then something else.”

He didn’t bother hiding the smile.

“Very specific.”

She opened the snack drawer. Yichen watched her retrieve a packet of seaweed crackers.

“That’s not lunch.”

“I know.”

She opened another drawer and found a packet of instant noodles. He raised an eyebrow.

“Xiaoran.”

“What?”

“We have proper food.”

“I know.”

“Then why are you eating snacks?”

She met his eyes.

“Because we’re having an unproductive Sunday.”

He laughed.

“Is that what we’re calling it?”

“Yes.”

He took the packet from her and placed it on the counter.

“How about I make something?”

Her expression brightened.

“Really?”

“Yes. But you’re helping.”

She nodded enthusiastically.

“Of course.”

Yichen made a quick lunch while Xiaoran prepared the vegetables. Or rather, she prepared some of them.

The rest of the time, she stood beside him, occasionally stealing small pieces of food.

He caught her reaching for a piece of chicken.

“That’s hot.”

She withdrew her hand.

“I know.”

“Then wait.”

She turned to him.

“Can I have a kiss while I wait?”

He turned towards her.

“You’re very demanding today.”

She smiled. He leaned down and kissed her. Then he returned to the stove.

Xiaoran waited approximately thirty seconds before stealing another piece. Yichen didn’t even turn around.

“Xiaoran.”

She froze.

“How did you know?”

“I can hear you.”

She laughed. After lunch, they finally started cleaning the living room. Yichen vacuumed. Xiaoran wiped the coffee table. They were doing quite well.

Until Xiaoran found the television remote under the sofa.

“Yichen!”

He turned off the vacuum.

“What?”

“Look what I found.”

He looked at the remote.

“Good.”

“It was missing yesterday.”

“Yes.”

She pressed a button. The television turned on. A drama appeared on the screen. Xiaoran looked at it, then at Yichen. He already knew.

“No.”

“I didn’t say anything.”

“You were about to.”

That made her grin.

“Just one episode.”

“We’re cleaning.”

“One episode while we rest.”

“We haven’t finished.”

She walked towards him, holding the remote behind her back.

“Please?”

He looked at her. She widened her eyes. He sighed.

“How long?”

“Forty minutes.”

“That’s an episode.”

“Exactly.”

He considered the vacuum cleaner, then the television. Then her face.

“All right.”

She immediately smiled.

“You’re the best.”

He put the vacuum away.

“You’re taking advantage of me.”

She took his hand.

“Come on.”

One episode became two. Two became an argument about whether the male lead was being unnecessarily stubborn. Yichen thought he was. Xiaoran thought he was misunderstood.

They paused the drama several times to discuss it.

At one point, Xiaoran became so invested that she sat upright, gesturing at the screen.

“Look! Look at his expression! He obviously wants to explain!”

Yichen looked at her.

“He’s had three opportunities.”

“But he didn’t know what to say!”

“He could start with the truth.”

“That’s easy for you to say.”

Something in his face eased.

“Would you prefer I lie to you?”

She turned towards him.

“Of course not.”

“Then?”

“Then don’t compare real life to drama.”

He laughed. She leaned back against him.

“You’re too logical.”

“And you’re too forgiving.”

“That’s why we’re a good couple.”

He kissed the side of her head.

“Perhaps.”

When the second episode ended, Xiaoran stretched. Yichen looked at the clock.

“Three thirty.”

She followed his gaze, then slowly turned towards him.

“...Oh.”

“Yes.”

She looked towards the living room. The coffee table was clean. The floor wasn’t vacuumed. There was a laundry basket beside the sofa. The kitchen still needed attention. The wardrobe remained untouched. She sighed.

“We’re terrible.”

Yichen glanced at her.

“We’ve accomplished several things.”

“Like what?”

“We changed the bedsheets.”

She nodded.

“Yes.”

“We made lunch.”

“Yes.”

“We found the remote.”

She laughed.

“That’s not cleaning.”

“It was a significant discovery.”

She leaned against his shoulder.

“You’re making excuses.”

“Would you prefer I tell you we’re behind schedule?”

She held his gaze.

“No.”

He pressed a kiss into her hair.

“Then don’t worry.”

At four, they made snacks. This was entirely Xiaoran’s idea.

She had decided that if they were going to be unproductive, they might as well be properly unproductive.

They made popcorn, cut some fruit, and prepared two small plates of biscuits.

Yichen handled the popcorn while Xiaoran arranged the fruit. She was pleased with the result.

“Look.”

He glanced at the plate.

“Very nice.”

“I made it pretty.”

“I can see that.”

She placed a strawberry near the edge, then another.

Then she moved one because the arrangement looked uneven. Yichen watched her.

“Are we eating this or photographing it?”

“Both.”

She took a picture. Then she took another. Then she asked him to move his hand because it was in the frame. He moved it. She took another photograph. Finally, she looked satisfied.

“Done.”

Yichen picked up a strawberry. She slapped his hand lightly.

“Wait!”

He held her gaze.

“What?”

“I haven’t taken one of you holding it.”

He sighed, but his mouth was smiling.

“All right.”

She held out a strawberry. He took it between his fingers and looked towards the camera.

“Smile.”

He gave her a smile.

“More.”

He raised an eyebrow.

“Xiaoran.”

“Please.”

He leaned towards the camera, holding the strawberry near his mouth. She took the picture. Then she looked at it. Her eyes widened.

“Oh.”

“What?”

“You’re very handsome.”

He laughed.

“Thank you.”

She looked at the photograph again, then at him.

“Can I have another?”

He put the strawberry down. He held out his hand. She stepped closer.

He slipped one arm around her waist and kissed her cheek. She laughed.

“That’s not the picture I asked for.”

“Then take it.”

She raised her phone. But instead of taking the photograph, she turned her face and kissed him. Yichen smiled against her lips.

“You’re terrible at photography.”

“Why?”

“Because you keep forgetting to take the picture.”

She laughed. By early evening, they had accepted that the apartment wouldn’t be spotless.

The laundry had been washed and dried. The kitchen counters were clean. The living room had been vacuumed, eventually.

But the wardrobe remained untouched, and the bathroom still needed cleaning. Xiaoran stood in front of the whiteboard. She held the marker.

Yichen stood behind her, his arms loosely around her waist.

She crossed out several items, then stared at the remaining list.

“Look at this.”

He rested his chin against her head.

“Mm.”

“We didn’t finish.”

“No.”

“At all.”

“We did some things.”

She looked at him.

“Are you not disappointed?”

He considered it.

“Not particularly.”

“Why?”

He turned her gently towards him.

“Because it’s Sunday.”

“That’s your explanation?”

“Yes.”

He moved her hair off her cheek.

“We have the rest of the week to clean. I’d rather spend today with you.”

Her expression softened.

“You say that now, but tomorrow you’ll be looking for your missing socks.”

“I can survive.”

“And the bathroom?”

“Can wait.”

“The wardrobe?”

“Also.”

She smiled.

“You’re a bad influence.”

Yichen leaned down and kissed her.

“Am I?”

She nodded.

“Very.”

He kissed her again, a little longer this time. When he pulled away, she was smiling.

“Maybe we should make a new plan.”

“What kind?”

She looked at the whiteboard, then at him.

“Next Sunday, we clean properly.”

“All right.”

“And no distractions.”

“Agreed.”

She gave him a suspicious look.

“You’re agreeing too easily.”

That got a smile out of him.

“Do you want me to disagree?”

She laughed.

“No.”

He kissed her.

“Then it’s settled.”

At night, Xiaoran was already in bed when Yichen finished locking the balcony door.

He turned off the bedroom lights, leaving only the bedside lamp on.

She was sitting against the headboard, wearing one of his shirts and holding her phone. She reached for him. Yichen climbed into bed.

She immediately moved towards him, settling against his side. He pulled the blanket over them. He kissed her temple. She tilted her head.

“Yichen.”

“Hm?”

“Did you enjoy today?”

He didn’t bother hiding the smile.

“Yes.”

She laughed.

“That’s terrible.”

He brushed his thumb over her cheek.

“We had breakfast together. We changed the sheets. We made lunch. We watched television. We made snacks.”

“And kissed.”

“Quite a lot.”

She grinned.

“That’s important.”

“Very.”

She rested her head against his chest. For a while, neither spoke. Then Xiaoran lifted her head.

“Wait.”

Yichen looked down.

“What?”

“We forgot the bathroom.”

He stared at her, then laughed.

“Xiaoran.”

“What?”

“Go to sleep.”

“But—”

“We’ll clean it tomorrow.”

She considered that, then smiled.

“Okay.”

She settled against him again. A few minutes passed.

Yichen thought she had fallen asleep when she spoke once more.

“Yichen?”

“Yes?”

“Next Sunday, let’s not make a schedule.”

He looked down at her.

“Why?”

“Because we never follow it.”

He laughed.

“That’s a reasonable conclusion.”

She smiled with her eyes closed.

“Maybe we should just do things slowly.”

He kissed her hair.

“That sounds better.”

She shifted closer, slipping one arm around his waist.

“And if we get distracted...”

“We get distracted.”

He smiled. She laughed.

“Goodnight.”

“Goodnight, Xiaoran.”

Yichen glanced once at the whiteboard visible through the open bedroom door.

16:00 — Rest.

They had missed that schedule by several hours. He smiled, turned off the bedside lamp, and pulled her a little closer.

chapters.desc: Her father still hasn’t quite said what he thinks of Yichen. Then there is a note under the rice cooker.
chapters.title: The Note Under the Rice Cooker
chapters.epigraph: “And he said I should look after you.”
chapters.content:
Zhou Yichen had been to the Lins’ flat often enough by now to know where everything was. He knew which cupboard had the tea, which drawer had the spare chopsticks, and which floorboard by the kitchen clicked when you stepped on it. He knew that Mrs. Lin would ask whether he’d eaten whether he arrived five minutes after lunch or five minutes before dinner.

What he still hadn’t worked out was Xiaoran’s father.

It wasn’t that Mr. Lin was unfriendly. He was warm, and easy, and had always been kind to him. They could talk about basketball, or the news, or the water bureau’s ongoing feud with the city’s drainage department. Sometimes Mr. Lin asked him to help with small jobs around the flat. But there was something about him that made Yichen careful. Perhaps because he respected him. Or perhaps because he knew exactly how much Xiaoran meant to him, and understood that loving a man’s daughter wasn’t quite the same thing as being welcomed into his house.

They took the early train up from Shanghai on a Saturday in March and were at the door by half past eleven. Mrs. Lin opened it.

“Yichen! Come in. Have you eaten?”

“Not yet, Auntie.”

“Good. I’ve made too much.”

“You said that last time!” Xiaoran called, already past her mother and halfway down the hall with her shoes off.

“Because you didn’t eat enough last time!”

Yichen smiled and stepped in and held out the bag of fruit. Mrs. Lin looked inside.

“Strawberries. In March.”

“Xiaoran said you’d been wanting them.”

“Xiaoran says a lot of things,” said Mrs. Lin, and carried them off to the kitchen looking pleased.

✦ ✦ ✦

Lunch was noisy in the comfortable way family lunches were. Mr. Lin sat at the end of the table and asked about the Herons’ game the week before, which he had watched on his phone in bed with the sound off so as not to wake his wife, and Yichen told him about the new defensive scheme and the trip to Qingdao coming up.

“You’re training every day?”

“Most days, Uncle. It depends on the schedule.”

“Don’t overdo it.”

“I won’t.”

“He says that,” said Xiaoran, “but sometimes he comes home so tired he falls asleep before dinner.”

“That happened once.”

“Twice.”

“Once and a half.”

“How do you fall asleep half a time?”

“Leave him alone. It’s not easy, playing at that level. Eat,” said her father. He put a piece of fish in Yichen’s bowl without looking.

After lunch, Mrs. Lin summoned Xiaoran into the bedroom to help with something in the wardrobe, and Xiaoran protested that she had only just finished eating, and went anyway, dragging her feet. Mr. Lin stayed in the living room with Yichen.

“Can you help me with something?”

“Of course, Uncle.”

“The rice cooker. I think the plug’s working loose. Will you take a look?”

It was nothing. The plug hadn’t been pushed all the way into the socket, and the cord had got shoved behind the cabinet. Yichen pulled it out, reseated the plug, checked the light came on, and tucked the cord back neatly.

“There. It should be fine now.”

“Good. Thank you.”

He was turning to go back to the living room when he noticed a small folded square of paper under the rice cooker, wedged beneath one of its rubber feet.

“Uncle, is this yours?”

Mr. Lin looked over. Then, casually: “Ah. That’s for you.”

Yichen went still. “For me?”

“Yes.”

He looked at the paper. On the outside, in Mr. Lin’s square handwriting, it said For Yichen.

Mr. Lin had already turned on the tap and was washing his hands. “Read it when you’ve got time.”

“All right, Uncle.”

He didn’t open it. He folded it back along its crease and put it in his pocket, carefully, and went back into the living room with absolutely no idea what to expect.

✦ ✦ ✦

Xiaoran found him on the sofa twenty minutes later and sat down beside him with a bowl of cut strawberries.

“Why are you sitting here on your own?”

“Your father asked me to look at the rice cooker.”

“And?”

“It’s working.”

“Then why do you look so serious?”

“Maybe I’m tired.”

“You’ve been here an hour.”

“A very tiring hour,” he said, and she laughed and leaned against him and fed him a strawberry. Then she noticed the white corner sticking out of his pocket.

“What’s that?”

“Something your father gave me.”

She sat bolt upright. “What?”

“A note.”

“A note?”

“Yes.”

“What does it say?”

“I haven’t read it.”

“Why not?”

“He told me to read it when I had time.”

She stared at him. “You’re telling me my father gave you a mysterious note and you haven’t opened it?”

“That’s right.”

“Why are you so calm?”

“Should I be worried?”

“Maybe!”

“Do you know what it says?”

“No!”

“Then how do you know I should be worried?”

“Because it’s from my father,” she said, and reached for his pocket.

He caught her wrist. “Don’t.”

“Let me see.”

“It’s addressed to me.”

“He’s my father!”

“And?”

“And I grew up in this flat!”

“That doesn’t make it your letter.”

She looked at him in total disbelief. “You’re choosing a piece of paper over me?”

“At the moment, yes,” he said, and kissed her temple before she could say anything else.

✦ ✦ ✦

For the rest of the afternoon she couldn’t leave it alone.

“Did he say anything else when he gave it to you?”

“No.”

“Did he look serious?”

“A bit.”

“Did he smile?”

“Yes.”

“Was it a normal smile or a suspicious smile?”

He looked at her. “How many kinds of smile does your father have?”

“Several.”

He thought about it. “Then perhaps the suspicious one.”

“What?”

“I’m teasing.”

She hit his arm. He caught her hand and held it.

“How am I supposed to relax? My father has written you a secret letter.”

“Maybe it’s a shopping list.”

“Then why isn’t my name on it?”

“Maybe he doesn’t want you knowing what vegetables he needs.”

“You’re not taking this seriously.”

“I am.”

“You’re enjoying it.”

“That’s also true. Xiaoran. If your father wanted you to read it, he’d have given it to you.” He pulled her in against his side.

She was quiet. It was a reasonable answer. She hated it, but it was reasonable.

“Then let him have his conversation with me,” he said.

She put her head down on his shoulder. “All right. But if it’s something bad, you have to tell me.” A few seconds passed.

“I’ll tell you,” he said.

✦ ✦ ✦

It was nearly five when he read it. Xiaoran was in her old bedroom looking for a cardigan. Mrs. Lin had gone down to the shop. Mr. Lin was out on the balcony watering his chili plants with his back to the room. Yichen sat at the dining table, took the paper out of his pocket, and unfolded it.

The handwriting was a little uneven, but careful. It wasn’t long.

Yichen,

Thank you for always treating Xiaoran well.

She is a bit stubborn. She doesn’t always say when she’s tired, and sometimes she acts as if everything is fine when it isn’t.

I know she can look after herself. We brought her up to.

But I hope you’ll keep looking after each other.

You don’t have to be perfect. Just be honest with each other, and don’t let small things turn into big ones because neither of you wants to speak first.

And when things are hard, remember you can always come here.

You are welcome in this house.

He sat still. He read the last line again.

He didn’t quite know why a few sentences on a square of paper had done what they’d done to him. Perhaps because there was nothing in it about money, or expectations, or what kind of future he ought to provide. Mr. Lin hadn’t asked him to promise anything impossible. He had said that his daughter could stand on her own two feet, and asked him to stand beside her. And then that last line.

He looked towards the kitchen, where the rice cooker sat on the counter with its little red light on. Out on the balcony, Mr. Lin was still watering the same plant, for much longer than a chili plant needed.

Yichen folded the note and put it back in his pocket.

✦ ✦ ✦

Xiaoran came out of her bedroom in a cardigan from her last year of high school, a bit too small for her now, and came and stood behind his chair and put her chin on his shoulder.

“Are you ready to go?”

“In a minute.”

“Did you read it?”

“Yes.”

“And?”

“And what?”

“What does it say?”

“Nothing,” he said.

She straightened up. “Nothing?”

“Nothing important.”

“Then why did he write your name on it?”

“So I wouldn’t mistake it for someone else’s.”

“Yichen.”

He laughed. She came round the chair and stood in front of him with the expression she always wore when she wanted something and had decided being cute would be more effective than arguing. It usually was. He reached up and took her hand.

“It’s between your father and me.”

Her face softened a little. “Is it about me?”

“Yes.”

“What did he say?”

He stood up and pushed her hair back off her cheek. “He said you’re stubborn.”

Her mouth fell open. “That’s it?”

“Among other things.”

“What other things?”

“That you don’t always say when you’re tired. And that you sometimes pretend everything’s fine.”

“That’s not true.”

“Not always,” she admitted.

“And he said I should look after you.”

She didn’t say anything. “He said that?”

“Yes.”

She looked down at their hands. “What else?”

He thought about telling her. He decided not to. “That’s all you’re getting.”

“Why?”

“Because he gave it to me.”

“You’re a vault.”

“Apparently.”

“Is it something embarrassing?”

“Perhaps.”

“Yichen!”

He laughed and bent down and kissed her hair. “Your father likes me.”

She went still. “That’s what it says?”

“That’s what I understood.”

She studied his face. He was smiling, but there was something quieter underneath, something she couldn’t quite read. She didn’t push. She just wrapped her arms round him, there by the dining table, and held on.

“Of course he likes you. He’s liked you for ages,” she said into his chest.

“I know.”

“He’s probably more comfortable with you than with me.”

“That would be concerning,” he said, and rested his chin on her hair, and they stood like that until they heard the balcony door slide open and she let go fast.

✦ ✦ ✦

When they were leaving, Mr. Lin came to the door with them.

“Going already?”

“Yes, Uncle. Thank you for lunch.”

“Come again.”

“I will.”

Mr. Lin looked at him. “Did you read it?”

“Yes, Uncle.”

A small pause. “All right.”

Xiaoran was bent over in the doorway doing up her shoes. Yichen dropped his voice so she wouldn’t hear. “Thank you.”

Mr. Lin looked at him for a second longer, and nodded once. “Look after each other.”

“We will.”

Xiaoran straightened up. “What are you two whispering about?”

“Nothing,” said her father.

“Nothing important,” said Yichen.

She looked from one to the other, deeply suspicious. Her father patted her on the shoulder. “Go on. Don’t keep him waiting. Message me when you’re home.”

“Bye, Dad.”

“Goodbye, Uncle.”

“Goodbye, Yichen.”

✦ ✦ ✦

They walked to the station with her hand in his coat pocket. For a while she didn’t say anything.

“Are you going to keep it? The note,” she said eventually.

“Yes.”

“Why?”

He thought about it. “Because it’s important.”

“Even though you won’t tell me what it says?”

“Because I won’t tell you,” he said, and she groaned and leaned her whole weight on his arm.

“You’re so annoying.”

He said, “Your father’s a good man. He trusts you to make your own decisions. And he trusts me to be next to you while you make them.”

She slowed down. He slowed with her.

“Did he really say that?”

“Something like that.”

She was quiet for a few steps. Then: “I think he wrote something embarrassing.”

“Why?”

“Because you keep smiling every time I ask.”

“Maybe I just like you.”

It wasn’t an answer, and they both knew it.

“It’s the one you’re getting,” he said, and she laughed and squeezed his hand inside the pocket.

That night, back in their flat in Shanghai, she messaged him from the bedroom while he was still reading on the sofa, nine metres away, because she had decided this was a conversation best had in writing.

Xiaoran: I still think Dad wrote something embarrassing

Yichen: You think too much.

Xiaoran: you’re hiding something

Yichen: Perhaps.

Xiaoran: I’m going to ask him tomorrow

Yichen: You can try.

Xiaoran: good night, traitor

He put his phone down and went into the bedroom. She was already asleep, on his side of the bed again, with her phone still in her hand. He took it out of her fingers and put it on the charger. Then he opened the drawer on his side, and put the note in, under the ticket stubs from his father and the first page of his Herons contract, where he kept the papers that had changed something.

He didn’t tell her what it said for another year.

chapters.desc: He meant to watch game footage. She has ceramic cats, a duck in a knitted hat and twenty minutes of things to show him.
chapters.title: A Little Too Close
chapters.epigraph: “Because someone kept showing me ceramic cats.”
chapters.content:
Yichen had been sitting on the sofa for nearly forty minutes.

He had finished training earlier than usual, showered, changed into a dark T-shirt and comfortable trousers, and settled down with his tablet to review some footage from the previous Herons game. It was supposed to be a quiet evening. Then Xiaoran came home.

She greeted him with a kiss on the cheek, complained about a colleague who had sent her a file in the wrong format, stole two pieces of fruit from the kitchen, and disappeared into the bedroom to change.

When she returned, she had her phone in one hand and a sudden abundance of things to show him.

“Yichen.”

“Hm?”

“Look at this.”

He paused the footage. Xiaoran stood beside the sofa, holding her phone out. It was a picture of a little ceramic cat she’d found online.

“Isn’t this cute?”

He glanced at the screen.

“Very cute.”

“Look at its expression.”

He looked again.

“It looks unhappy.”

“Exactly! It’s so funny. I think it looks like you when you’re concentrating.”

Yichen raised his eyes.

“Does it?”

“Yes. Look. The little eyes. The mouth. Everything.” She zoomed in on the cat’s face.

He studied the picture.

“Do I really look like that?”

“Sometimes.”

“That’s unfortunate.”

She laughed. Then, instead of sitting down beside him, she leaned over the back of the sofa, bringing her face close to his so she could show him another picture.

“And look at this one. It’s the same artist.”

Yichen tilted his head to see the screen. A second ceramic cat appeared.

“That one’s better,” he said.

“Why?”

“It looks less angry.”

“You’re saying I’m wrong about you?”

“I’m saying the first one is more handsome.”

Xiaoran burst into laughter. She was still leaning over him when she began scrolling through the artist’s other works. Her hair fell forward, brushing his shoulder. One hand rested on the back of the sofa, and her phone was held just beside his face. Yichen returned his attention to the screen. Or tried to.

“Wait, wait. This one!”

She moved the phone closer. He looked. A little ceramic duck wearing a knitted hat.

“Do you think we should buy it?”

“No.”

“Why not?”

“Where would you put it?”

“On the shelf.”

“The shelf is full.”

“We can make space.”

“You said that about the other duck.”

“That duck is different.”

“How?”

She paused. Then she looked at him with great seriousness.
